recommendations: Build the rice on Quickshell 0.3.x taken from each distro's own repo: `pacman -S quickshell` on Arch (0.3.1) and nixpkgs-unstable `quickshell` (0.3.1) on NixOS. Both machines then run the same QML API. Avoid quickshell-git unless you adopt caelestia or DMS's flake, since Arch -git builds break on Qt updates.

Write your own config instead of adopting a full rice, and borrow structure from caelestia and DMS. Suggested layout: shell.qml; services/ for Singleton wrappers (Audio, Media, Battery, Hypr, Notifs); modules/ for bar, osd, notifications, launcher (DesktopEntries.applications), dashboard, lock and session; components/ for animated primitives. For popups, consider caelestia's approach: one fullscreen top-layer PanelWindow per screen with a Region mask and HyprlandFocusGrab, so panels can slide out of the bar smoothly.

Standardise on Hyprland's Lua config on both machines (0.56.2 on Arch and nixpkgs-unstable). In QML use HyprlandWorkspace.activate(), or branch on Hyprland.usingLua before calling Hyprland.dispatch(). Give each surface its own WlrLayershell.namespace and add blur and animation with hl.layer_rule. Only use Quickshell's BackgroundEffect if both machines run Hyprland 0.56+ (nixos-26.05 has 0.55.4).

For the cute, animated look, use QtQuick Behavior/NumberAnimation with Easing.OutBack or springy curves, MultiEffect/shaders, and matugen for wallpaper-based colours. Keep all animations in shared components so timings stay consistent.

Deploy the same config directory on both distros. On Arch, symlink it into ~/.config/quickshell/<name> with stow or chezmoi. On NixOS, use Home Manager `programs.quickshell.configs` for reproducible builds, or an out-of-store symlink while developing so hot reload still works (store paths are read-only). Add `//@ pragma ShellId <name>` so state and cache paths do not change when symlink paths change, which v0.3.0 made matter.

Make it testable without real hardware:
- Give every service singleton a mock or fake mode switched by an environment variable (read with Quickshell.env()).
- Give each module a test.qml that hosts it in a FloatingWindow, copying the official lockscreen test.qml pattern.
- Script checks with `qs ipc call`, `qs ipc prop get` and `qs ipc wait`.
- Null-guard every service (UPower.displayDevice not initialised, Bluetooth.defaultAdapter null, no MPRIS players).
- Always test the lock screen in FloatingWindow mode before using WlSessionLock.

If you would rather not build it yourself, DankMaterialShell is the most portable ready-made Quickshell shell (Arch extra, nixpkgs module and flake modules), though its Material 3 look needs restyling to feel cute. Caelestia looks the most polished but is Hyprland-only and needs git and AUR dependencies. end-4 is not a good fit because NixOS is only a community work in progress. Noctalia v5 is solid but can no longer be customised in QML.

Keep the Waybar + swaync + swayosd + rofi 2.0 stack only as a fallback or safe mode. Watch for the Hyprland Lua dispatch bug on workspace clicks, and skip wlogout (unmaintained since 2024). Avoid eww, Ignis (Rust rewrite pending) and Fabric (pre-alpha) for a new build. AGS v3 is viable, but nixpkgs is behind and Astal's Hyprland library is not Lua-aware.
deprecations_pitfalls: Quickshell v0.2.0: `root:/` imports were replaced by `import qs.<path>`; relative paths outside the shell directory are rejected; `Quickshell.shellRoot`, `configDir` and `configPath` became `shellDir` / `shellPath()`; QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE is ignored unless `//@ pragma RespectSystemStyle` is set; and PanelWindow's Auto exclusion now reserves space for single-anchor panels.

Quickshell v0.3.0 stopped canonicalizing config paths, so the shell id comes from the symlink path. Nix and Home Manager configs behind symlinks may get new state and cache directories. Pin it with `//@ pragma ShellId`.
Setting QsWindow width/height is deprecated; use implicitWidth/implicitHeight. Window `color` defaults to white, so set `color: "transparent"` on bars and OSDs.
`//@ pragma` lines are only read before the first `import` line. Tray menus (SystemTrayItem.display()) need `//@ pragma UseQApplication`, otherwise Quickshell logs a critical error.
`qs msg` is deprecated; use `qs ipc call`. IpcHandler functions need explicit types (string, int, bool, real, color) and take at most 10 arguments.

Pipewire nodes must be bound with PwObjectTracker before reading `.audio.volume` or `.audio.muted`. MprisPlayer.position does not update on its own; drive positionChanged() with a Timer or FrameAnimation. UPowerDevice.percentage is 0–1, not 0–100.

WlSessionLock: if Quickshell crashes or exits without `locked = false`, the compositor keeps the screen locked with a solid colour. WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive is not a lock screen. Test the lock with a FloatingWindow first and keep a TTY escape plan.

GlobalShortcut appid+name pairs must be unique. Two Quickshell instances, or xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland (XDPH), registering the same pair can crash the last client to register. Launch with `qs -n` (no-duplicate).

Only one process can own org.freedesktop.Notifications. Stop mako, dunst or swaync before using NotificationServer. NotificationServer drops notifications unless the notification handler sets `tracked = true`.

Hyprland 0.55+ in Lua mode treats IPC dispatch strings as Lua, so legacy `dispatch workspace N` fails. This breaks Waybar 0.15.0 workspace clicks and probably Astal/AGS. Scripts must use `hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = N })'`. hyprlang is supported for only 1–2 releases after 0.55.

The official quickshell-examples focus_following_panel uses the old `/tmp/hypr/$SIG/.socket2.sock` path. Use the Quickshell.Hyprland module (Hyprland.eventSocketPath) instead of hard-coded socket paths.

nixos-26.05 ships Quickshell 0.3.0 and Hyprland 0.55.4, while Arch and nixpkgs-unstable have 0.3.1 and 0.56.2. For identical behaviour on both machines, track nixpkgs-unstable (or pin the flake) on NixOS.

DMS on Arch uses the release `quickshell`, but its Nix flake builds Quickshell from source because it relies on unreleased features, so behaviour can differ between the two machines. Caelestia requires quickshell-git on both, plus qt6-m3shapes-git from the AUR.
Noctalia v5 (noctalia-dev/noctalia) is a native C++ rewrite, not Quickshell. The old noctalia-shell v4 QML, including tutorials and forks, is unmaintained, and v4 settings are not migrated.

nixpkgs `ags` is still 2.3.0, while upstream AGS v3 uses a completely different Gnim/JSX API; use the upstream flake. nixpkgs `rofi-wayland` now throws an error; use `rofi` 2.0.0. Arch also ships only `rofi` (2.0.0 with Wayland).
The AUR's quickshell-git (and any -git QML shell) can break after Arch Qt upgrades until it is rebuilt.

Quickshell's docs have moved to quickshell.org (quickshell.outfoxxed.me is still referenced). Upstream git has two paths, git.outfoxxed.me/quickshell/quickshell and git.outfoxxed.me/outfoxxed/quickshell (the latter is used in the flake instructions).

findings.claim: matugen latest release is 4.2.0 (2026-08-05). It is in Arch [extra] as 4.2.0, AUR matugen-bin 4.2.0, and nixpkgs master (pkgs.matugen) 4.2.0. License is GPL-2.0-or-later.
findings.detail: 4.2.0 added scheme-smart plus a smart mode, `source_color_index` in the config, a per-template scheme-type cache and an `enabled` key on templates. 4.1.0 (2026-03-22) added the `contrast` config option, per-template `type`, `--opacity`, and `alpha_hex`/`alpha_hex_stripped`. 4.0.0 (2026-02-12) added base16 generation, changed the default JSON output (the old format is available with `--old-json-output`), added the `format` filter, `not` in if-statements and `--source-color-index`.
findings.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InioX/matugen/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InioX/matugen/HEAD/Cargo.toml ; crates.io API ; archlinux.org packages JSON ; nixpkgs pkgs/by-name/ma/matugen/package.nix

findings.claim: matugen color keyword syntax is {{ colors.<name>.<mode>.<format> }}. <mode> is default, dark or light. `default` means whichever mode was chosen with -m.
findings.detail: Formats: hex (#RRGGBB), hex_stripped (RRGGBB), hex_alpha (#RRGGBBAA), hex_alpha_stripped, alpha_hex (#AARRGGBB), alpha_hex_stripped, rgb, rgba (rgba(r, g, b, 1.0)), hsl, hsla, red, green, blue, alpha, hue, saturation, lightness. Other roots: base16.base00..base0f.<mode>.<format>, palettes.<primary|secondary|tertiary|error|neutral|neutral_variant>._<tone>.hex (for example palettes.error._99.hex), plus {{image}}, {{mode}} and {{is_dark_mode}}. Blocks use <* *>: `<* for name, value in colors *>`, `<* if {{ is_dark_mode }} *> <* else *> <* endif *>`, `<* if not ... *>`, `<* include "tpl" *>`, loop.index/loop.first/loop.last, and numeric ranges like `-10..10`. Filters are chained with | (lighten, set_alpha, set_lightness, saturate, blend, harmonize, invert, grayscale, auto_lightness, to_color, format, replace, to_upper/to_lower). Escape a literal with \{{ .

findings.claim: matugen scheme types on the CLI are -t/--type scheme-content|scheme-expressive|scheme-fidelity|scheme-fruit-salad|scheme-monochrome|scheme-neutral|scheme-rainbow|scheme-tonal-spot|scheme-vibrant|scheme-smart. The default is scheme-tonal-spot. Mode is -m/--mode dark|light|smart and defaults to dark.
findings.detail: Inside config.toml, the per-template `type` uses PascalCase instead: "SchemeExpressive", "SchemeTonalSpot", "SchemeSmart" and so on. Templates can also set their own `mode`. The Nix module uses the kebab-case names in `programs.matugen.type`. SchemeSmart has no Material variant mapping; it was added in 4.2.0.

findings.claim: The matugen config lives at ~/.config/matugen/config.toml. It has a [config] section, [config.wallpaper], [config.custom_colors] and one [templates.<name>] table per template.
findings.detail: [config] keys: version_check, caching, fallback_color, prefer (darkness|lightness|saturation|less-saturation|value|closest-to-fallback), expr_prefix/expr_postfix/block_prefix/block_postfix, import_json_files, contrast (-1..1), source_color_index (0-4). [config.wallpaper] keys: set, command, arguments, pre_hook. Template keys: input_path, output_path (a string or a list), input_path_modes = { dark=..., light=... }, mode, type, index (processing order), enabled, pre_hook, post_hook, expr_/block_ prefix overrides, and colors_to_compare + compare_to, which exposes {{closest_color}} to hooks. Hooks can use keywords such as {{image}}. Append `&` to make a hook async.

findings.claim: Since matugen 4.x, generating from an image can stop at an interactive source-color picker. Scripts must pass --source-color-index N or set `prefer`/`source_color_index` in config.toml.
findings.detail: From arguments.rs: 'Setting this to any value will not show the selection prompt. In earlier versions the default was 0.' end-4's switchwall.sh calls matugen with `--source-color-index 0`.

findings.claim: InioX/matugen-themes is the official template collection. It has ready templates and reload hooks for many apps.
findings.detail: Covered apps include hyprland (.conf and .lua), kitty, ghostty, foot, alacritty, wezterm, rofi, fuzzel, waybar/swaync (colors.css), GTK3/4, qt5ct/qt6ct, KDE .colors (for Darkly/Breeze), Kvantum, quickshell.json, pywalfox, spicetify (Sleek), Vesktop (midnight/system24), btop, cava, starship, neovim, dunst, mako, niri, sway, tmux, yazi, zathura, zed, vscode and papirus-folders. There is no SDDM, fzf or fastfetch template.

findings.claim: Hyprland 0.55+ uses Lua configuration (~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua). Hyprlang (hyprland.conf) is deprecated and will be supported for about 1-2 more releases. Arch currently ships Hyprland 0.56.2.
findings.detail: Border colors are set with hl.config({ general = { col = { active_border = { colors = {"rgba(..)","rgba(..)"}, angle = 45 }, inactive_border = "rgba(..)" } } }). Other files are loaded with require("file"). Home Manager's wayland.windowManager.hyprland.configType is "hyprlang" | "lua", and defaults to "lua" for home.stateVersion >= 26.05. matugen-themes ships hyprland-colors.lua, and end-4's illogical-impulse now generates a colors.lua that calls hl.config directly.

findings.claim: hyprlock (0.9.6 in Arch) is still configured with hyprlang in hyprlock.conf, so color templates for it stay in `$var = rgba(...)` form.
findings.detail: end-4 generates ~/.config/hypr/hyprlock/colors.conf with `$text_color = rgba({{colors.primary_fixed.default.hex_stripped}}FF)` and similar lines. hyprlock re-reads its config on every launch, so no reload step is needed.

findings.claim: swww has been renamed to awww and moved to Codeberg (codeberg.org/LGFae/awww). The latest release is 0.12.1.
findings.detail: The GitHub swww README says: 'This project has been renamed awww and moved to Codeberg' (blog post 2025-10-29). Release 0.12.0 made the rename and moved the cache to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/awww/$PKG_VERSION, which is a breaking change. 0.12.1 added --crop-gravity and pause/unpause. Packaging: Arch [extra] awww 0.12.1; nixpkgs pkgs.awww 0.12.1; `swww` in nixpkgs is now a warnAlias to awww (added 2026-03-22); Home Manager has services.awww with mkRenamedOptionModule from services.swww. Binaries are awww and awww-daemon, and env vars are AWWW_TRANSITION*. matugen's own example config already uses `awww img --transition-type center {{ image }}`.

findings.claim: awww img transition flags: -t/--transition-type, --transition-step, --transition-duration, --transition-fps, --transition-angle, --transition-pos, --transition-bezier, --transition-wave, --invert-y.
findings.detail: Transition types: none, simple (default), fade, left, right, top, bottom, wipe, wave, grow, center, any, outer, random. Defaults: step 90 (2 for simple), duration 3s (not used by simple), fps 30, angle 45, pos center, bezier .54,0,.34,.99, wave 20,20. Other flags: --resize no|crop|fit|stretch (default crop), --crop-gravity, --fill-color, -o outputs, -n namespace, -f filter (default Lanczos3). Subcommands include query (JSON output), clear, kill, clean-cache, pause/unpause. Needs wlr-layer-shell, so it does not work on GNOME.

findings.claim: hyprpaper 0.8.4 (Arch and nixpkgs) uses anonymous `wallpaper { monitor path fit_mode timeout order recursive }` blocks. The older preload/unload/reload/listloaded requests are gone.
findings.detail: `path` may be a directory; with `timeout` it becomes a slideshow and `order = random` shuffles it. fit_mode is contain|cover|tile|fill. Global options: splash, splash_offset, splash_opacity, ipc. The IPC call is `hyprctl hyprpaper wallpaper '[mon], [path], [fit_mode]'`, and `listactive` shows the current wallpapers. Home Manager services.hyprpaper.settings.wallpaper takes a list of attrsets. hyprpaper has no transitions.

findings.claim: wallust: the latest stable release is 3.5.x (crates.io 3.5.1; AUR and nixpkgs 3.5.2). The Codeberg master branch is 4.1.0-alpha, which breaks palette names.
findings.detail: v3 config (~/.config/wallust/wallust.toml): backend, color_space, palette (e.g. saliencedark, dark16, harddark...), check_contrast, saturation, alpha, [templates] name = { template = 'rel-path-in-~/.config/wallust/', target = '~/abs' }, [hooks]. v4-alpha drops color_space and replaces the palette variants with palette = salience|ansi|kmeans plus style = dark|light and use16cols, and adds [templated_hooks]. `wallust migrate` converts old configs. Templates use a minijinja (Jinja2 subset) syntax: {{color0}}..{{color15}}, {{background}}, {{foreground}}, {{cursor}}, {{wallpaper}}, {{alpha}}, and filters | strip, | rgb, | hexa, | xrgb, | lighten(0.2), | darken, | blend(color0), | complementary. Setting `pywal = true` on a template switches it to pywal {color0} syntax. The CLI is `wallust run img`.

findings.claim: pywal16 3.8.15 (PyPI 2026-04-11; AUR python-pywal16; nixpkgs pywal16). In nixpkgs, `pywal` is now an alias of pywal16 (added 2026-02-01).
findings.detail: Templates go in ~/.config/wal/templates/ and are written to ~/.cache/wal/ under the same name. The syntax is Python str.format: {color0}..{color15}, {background}, {foreground}, {cursor}, {alpha}, {wallpaper}, with modifiers .rgb, .rgba, .xrgba, .strip, .red/.green/.blue. Literal braces must be doubled. Flags include --backend, --cols16, --saturate, --contrast, --theme/-f, -l (light), -n (skip wallpaper), -s (skip terminals), -t (skip tty), -e (skip reload), -a alpha.

findings.claim: hellwal is a fast C palette generator: AUR hellwal 1.0.8, nixpkgs hellwal 1.0.7. Its template syntax is %%color1.hex%%.
findings.detail: Formats: .hex (no leading #), .rgb, .r/.g/.b, plus optional alpha=0.5. Chainable operations such as %% color1.saturate(0.2).lighten(0.1).hex %% (also darken, rotate, complement, invert, sepia, contrast, brightness). Default paths: templates in ~/.config/hellwal/templates, themes in ~/.config/hellwal/themes, output to ~/.cache/hellwal/. Flags: -i img [--random], -d/-l/-c, --neon-mode, --json, -t theme, --override-colors. The VERSION macro in the source reads "6.9.6", which looks like a placeholder, so use the package versions instead.

findings.claim: Stylix is now nix-community/stylix (docs at nix-community.github.io/stylix). It follows a rolling master branch, with release branches matching NixOS (e.g. release-26.05).
findings.detail: Set stylix.enable = true and stylix.base16Scheme = "${pkgs.base16-schemes}/share/themes/<name>.yaml" (anything mkSchemeAttrs accepts works). stylix.override patches individual colors. stylix.image sets the wallpaper, and if no scheme is declared Stylix generates one from the image, biased by stylix.polarity = dark|light. Colors are exposed as config.lib.stylix.colors (base08, withHashtag.base08, base08-dec-r, ...). Each target has stylix.targets.<t>.enable; stylix.autoEnable = false switches everything to opt-in. When used as a NixOS module, Home Manager integration is auto-imported (homeManagerIntegration.autoImport/followSystem).

findings.claim: Stylix targets available as of the current docs TOC. There is no SDDM, Quickshell or fastfetch target.
findings.detail: Targets include hyprland (with hyprpaper sub-target), hyprlock, waybar, rofi, fuzzel, kitty, foot, ghostty, alacritty, wezterm, gtk, qt, kde, firefox (also Floorp/LibreWolf), zen-browser, chromium, discord (vencord/vesktop/nixcord), spicetify, neovim, btop, cava, fzf, starship, mako, dunst, swaync, swaylock, regreet, lightdm, grub, limine, plymouth, noctalia-shell, dank-material-shell, vicinae, yazi, zathura, zed, vscode, tmux and more. Target-specific pitfalls: the firefox target needs stylix.targets.firefox.profileNames = [ ... ] or nothing is themed; qt target platform defaults to "qtct"; the gtk target has extraCss and flatpakSupport.enable.

findings.claim: Stylix has no matugen or runtime (no-rebuild) theming. Issue #2031 'Matugen / Material You Modules' is still open (opened 2025-11-26).
findings.detail: Stylix only changes colors on rebuild. To mix it with a runtime matugen workflow, the usual approach is to keep Stylix for fonts, cursor, boot/TTY/greeter and static apps, and set stylix.targets.<app>.enable = false for every app matugen writes.

findings.claim: catppuccin/nix: add the flake input github:catppuccin/nix (or github:catppuccin/nix/release-26.05) and import catppuccin.nixosModules.catppuccin and catppuccin.homeModules.catppuccin.
findings.detail: Global options: catppuccin.enable, catppuccin.autoEnable, catppuccin.flavor (latte|frappe|macchiato|mocha, default mocha), catppuccin.accent (default mauve), catppuccin.enableReleaseCheck. NixOS ports include sddm, grub, limine, plymouth, tty, cursors, fcitx5 and gtk. Home Manager ports include hyprland, hyprlock, kitty, ghostty, foot, fuzzel, rofi, waybar, btop, cava, fzf, starship, nvim, firefox/floorp/librewolf, vesktop, kvantum, qt5ct, mako, swaync, yazi, zed and more. The HM catppuccin.gtk module now only exposes icon.* options, so there is no GTK widget theme.

findings.claim: GTK3 and GTK4/libadwaita can be recolored by writing @define-color overrides to ~/.config/gtk-{3,4}.0/colors.css and adding @import 'colors.css'; to gtk.css. libadwaita still honors @define-color named colors, which remain until GTK5.
findings.detail: libadwaita 1.6+ exposes CSS variables (--accent-bg-color, --window-bg-color ...) whose defaults reference the old named colors, so @define-color overrides still propagate. GTK3 also needs the adw-gtk3 theme. matugen-themes reloads GTK3 with `gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme ""; gsettings set ... gtk-theme adw-gtk3-{{mode}}` and GTK4 by flipping color-scheme prefer-light and prefer-dark.

findings.claim: Qt apps are colored through qt6ct/qt5ct color schemes: either a qtct colors conf, or a KDE .colors file used with the Darkly or Breeze style. Kvantum is the alternative.
findings.detail: For qtct: write ~/.config/qt6ct/colors/matugen.conf and set color_scheme_path=... plus custom_palette=true in qt6ct.conf. For KDE .colors: write ~/.local/share/color-schemes/Matugen.colors and set style=Darkly. Both need QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt6ct. Arch/AUR packages: qt6ct-kde 0.11, darkly 0.5.39. If qt libraries change, qt6ct-kde must be rebuilt. For Kvantum, matugen writes ~/.config/Kvantum/matugen/matugen.{kvconfig,svg} and kvantum.kvconfig sets theme=matugen.
findings.source: matugen-themes README (Qt, Kvantum sections) ; AUR RPC

findings.claim: Live-reload signals for runtime palette changes.
findings.detail: kitty: SIGUSR1 reloads config, or `kitten themes --reload-in=all Name`. Ghostty 1.2+: SIGUSR2 reloads config. foot: config is NOT reloaded at runtime; SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2 only switch between [colors-dark] and [colors-light]. The old [colors]/[colors2] sections were deprecated in 1.26.0 and removed in 1.28.0. Waybar: SIGUSR2 reloads by default, or set reload_style_on_change. btop: SIGUSR2 hot-reloads config. cava: SIGUSR1 does a full reload, SIGUSR2 reloads colors only. mako: makoctl reload. dunst: dunstctl reload. swaync: swaync-client -rs. Neovim: pkill -SIGUSR1 nvim plus an autocmd on the Signal event. rofi, fuzzel, hyprlock and starship re-read their config on every launch or prompt.
findings.source: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/conf/ ; kitty docs/kittens/themes.rst ; https://ghostty.org/docs/install/release-notes/1-2-0 ; https://codeberg.org/dnkl/foot/raw/branch/master/CHANGELOG.md ; Waybar man/waybar.5.scd.in ; btop src/btop.cpp + CHANGELOG ; cava README ; matugen-themes README

findings.claim: Quickshell (0.3.1 in Arch and nixpkgs) can pick up a matugen-written JSON palette live using FileView { watchChanges: true; onFileChanged: reload() } with a JsonAdapter.
findings.detail: The matugen-themes quickshell.json template writes md3, palette and base16 objects to ~/.local/state/quickshell/generated/colors.json, and a Colors.qml singleton binds to them. end-4 illogical-impulse writes ~/.local/state/quickshell/user/generated/colors.json the same way.
findings.source: matugen-themes README (Quickshell) + templates/quickshell.json ; https://git.outfoxxed.me/quickshell/quickshell/raw/branch/master/src/io/fileview.hpp ; end-4 dots matugen config.toml

findings.claim: How top shells derive their palette: end-4 illogical-impulse and DankMaterialShell use matugen, caelestia uses its own caelestia-cli, and Noctalia v4 (Quickshell) is no longer maintained in favor of a non-Qt v5.
findings.detail: end-4: matugen config.toml writes quickshell colors.json, hypr colors.lua, hyprlock colors.conf, fuzzel, gtk3/gtk4 and KDE colors. Its switchwall.sh passes --source-color-index 0 plus --mode/--type, toggles adw-gtk3 via gsettings, and plays video wallpapers with mpvpaper. DMS README: 'Wallpaper-based color schemes ... using matugen and dank16'. caelestia: wallpaper switcher via `>wallpaper` in its launcher, reading ~/Pictures/Wallpapers. Noctalia docs say v4 (Quickshell) is no longer maintained, and the README describes v5 as built directly on Wayland and OpenGL ES with no Qt or GTK.
findings.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/end-4/dots-hyprland/HEAD/dots/.config/matugen/config.toml ; .../switchwall.sh ; AvengeMedia/DankMaterialShell README ; caelestia-dots/shell README ; https://docs.noctalia.dev ; noctalia-dev/noctalia-shell README

findings.claim: Firefox is themed at runtime with Pywalfox 2.9.0 (PyPI pywalfox; AUR python-pywalfox; nixpkgs pywalfox-native 2.9.0).
findings.detail: Run `pywalfox install` once, restart the browser, then run `pywalfox update` after each palette change. Pywalfox reads ~/.cache/wal/colors.json, and matugen-themes ships a pywalfox-colors.json template for that path. The dark/light setting inside the add-on must be set by hand. Forks need --manifest-path and --profile-path; Flatpak needs a wrapper script. A userChrome/userContent approach also exists (matugen firefox-colors.css plus website CSS, with toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets=true).

findings.claim: Discord via Vesktop 1.6.7: Vencord watches both quickCss.css and the themes directory with fs.watch, so rewriting either file restyles Discord live.
findings.detail: Paths: DATA_DIR = app userData (~/.config/vesktop), quickCss at ~/.config/vesktop/settings/quickCss.css, themes at ~/.config/vesktop/themes. matugen-themes writes midnight-discord.css or system24.css into ~/.config/vesktop/themes; enable the theme once in Vencord settings. Flatpak paths differ.

findings.claim: Spotify via spicetify-cli 2.45.1 (AUR): write the theme's color.ini with a [matugen] section, set current_theme and color_scheme, then apply without restarting Spotify.
findings.detail: matugen-themes writes ~/.config/spicetify/Themes/Sleek/color.ini. config-xpui.ini needs color_scheme = matugen and current_theme = Sleek. The hook is `pgrep -x spicetify > /dev/null || spicetify apply -n`. The spicetify docs list `apply --no-restart` and a `watch` command that auto-applies color.ini and user.css changes.
findings.source: matugen-themes README (Spicetify Sleek) ; https://spicetify.app/docs/cli/commands ; AUR RPC

findings.claim: fzf colors go through --color with element names, and FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS_FILE lets a generated file hold them. fastfetch accepts #RRGGBB colors since v2.42.0.
findings.detail: fzf elements: fg, bg, hl, fg+ (current-fg), bg+ (current-bg), hl+ (current-hl), info, prompt, pointer, marker, spinner, header, border, among others. fastfetch: hex works in JSONC color fields (display.color.keys/title, logo.color.1) and as {##RRGGBB} in format strings; @N is xterm-256 (v2.57.0).

findings.claim: SDDM cannot simply be rewritten per wallpaper. It runs as the sddm user and themes live in root-owned /usr/share/sddm/themes (a read-only store path on NixOS).
findings.detail: Projects that sync SDDM with matugen, such as ii-sddm-theme (end-4 look) and sddm-noctalia, install a sudoers rule or helper scripts. On NixOS, SDDM color is normally set at build time: catppuccin.sddm exists, Stylix has no SDDM target (only lightdm/regreet), and the alternative is a theme package that reads colors from a path outside the store.
findings.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/3d3f/ii-sddm-theme/HEAD/README.md ; https://github.com/Vorxiu/sddm-noctalia ; Stylix TOC ; catppuccin/nix options list

findings.claim: Animated wallpaper options: mpvpaper 1.9 plays videos through mpv; linux-wallpaperengine plays Steam Wallpaper Engine scenes but needs an owned copy of Wallpaper Engine for its assets.
findings.detail: mpvpaper usage: `mpvpaper [-o "mpv opts"] <output|ALL> <file>`, with IPC via -o input-ipc-server=/tmp/mpv-socket and socat. linux-wallpaperengine flags: --screen-root <out> --bg <id|path>, --screen-span, --scaling stretch|fit|fill|default, --fps, --silent, --assets-dir, --no-fullscreen-pause, --fullscreen-pause-only-active (Wayland). On Wayland it needs wlr-layer-shell. Packages: AUR mpvpaper 1.9 and linux-wallpaperengine-git; nixpkgs mpvpaper 1.9 and linux-wallpaperengine.

findings.claim: Wallpaper picker UIs: waypaper 2.9 (AUR; nixpkgs 2.8) is a GTK front-end for awww/swww/hyprpaper/swaybg/mpvpaper/gslapper/linux-wallpaperengine/feh/xwallpaper, with a post_command hook.
findings.detail: Config keys in [Settings]: folder, wallpaper, backend, monitors, fill, subfolders, use_xdg_state, swww_transition_type/_step/_angle/_duration/_fps, post_command (expands $wallpaper and $monitor). `waypaper --restore` restores the last wallpaper on login. rofi 2.0.0 grid pickers use dmenu rows of the form `name\0icon\x1f/path/thumb` with -show-icons. Quickshell shells (end-4, DMS, caelestia) ship built-in pickers that call matugen themselves.

findings.claim: matugen's upstream Nix module (inputs.matugen.nixosModules.default, which defines programs.matugen.*) renders templates at build time and does NOT symlink the results.
findings.detail: Options include programs.matugen.{enable, wallpaper, source_color, templates.<n>.{input_path,output_path,pre_hook,post_hook}, custom_colors, type (scheme-*), variant, contrast, lightness_dark/light, source_color_index, jsonFormat}. It is useful for a reproducible default palette. Runtime switching still needs the matugen CLI writing into non-HM-managed files. Home Manager has no programs.matugen module of its own, but it does ship programs.wallust and programs.pywal.
findings.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InioX/matugen/HEAD/module.nix ; matugen README (NixOS section) ; home-manager module paths (HTTP 200/404 checks)

verified_examples.title: matugen ~/.config/matugen/config.toml (assembled from verified per-app entries)
verified_examples.code:
[config]
version_check = false
# avoid the interactive source-color prompt in scripts (4.x)
source_color_index = 0
fallback_color = "#ffbf9b"

[config.wallpaper]
set = true
command = "awww img --transition-type center {{ image }}"

[templates.hyprland]
input_path = '~/.config/matugen/templates/hyprland-colors.lua'
output_path = '~/.config/hypr/colors.lua'

[templates.kitty]
input_path = '~/.config/matugen/templates/kitty-colors.conf'
output_path = '~/.config/kitty/themes/Matugen.conf'
post_hook = "kitty +kitten themes --reload-in=all Matugen"

[templates.ghostty]
input_path = '~/.config/matugen/templates/ghostty'
output_path = '~/.config/ghostty/themes/Matugen'

recommendations: Use matugen 4.2.0 as the single runtime palette engine on both Arch and NixOS. Base the setup on InioX/matugen-themes templates and always run it non-interactively: `matugen image -m dark -t scheme-tonal-spot --source-color-index 0`, or set `source_color_index`/`prefer` in config.toml.

Write Hyprland colors as a generated Lua file (hl.config in the style of end-4's colors.lua) and load it from hyprland.lua with require(). Hyprland 0.55+ deprecated hyprlang, Arch already ships 0.56.2, and Home Manager defaults configType to "lua" for stateVersion 26.05. Add a `hyprctl reload` post_hook if required files are not auto-watched; that behavior was not verified. Keep hyprlock on hyprlang with `source = colors.conf`.

Use awww, not swww, for wallpapers with transitions: Arch `awww`, nixpkgs `pkgs.awww`, Home Manager `services.awww`. Set it as matugen's [config.wallpaper] command or call it from the picker script. Use hyprpaper only if you do not need transitions, and mpvpaper or linux-wallpaperengine for animated wallpapers, running matugen on an extracted frame.

On NixOS, split ownership. Use Stylix or catppuccin/nix for build-time-only surfaces: fonts, cursor, GRUB/limine, plymouth, TTY, SDDM (catppuccin.sddm). For every app matugen writes, set stylix.targets.<app>.enable = false or leave the catppuccin port off. Let Home Manager manage only stub configs that include or @import the generated files (gtk.css -> @import 'colors.css'; waybar style.css -> @import "colors.css"; kitty.conf include; foot.ini include; rofi @import "colors.rasi"). Never let Home Manager own the generated file paths.

Choose one reload hook per app: kitty `kitten themes --reload-in=all` or SIGUSR1, ghostty SIGUSR2, waybar SIGUSR2, btop SIGUSR2, cava SIGUSR1, nvim SIGUSR1 with a Signal autocmd, mako `makoctl reload`, swaync `swaync-client -rs`, GTK via the gsettings toggle scripts, Firefox `pywalfox update`, Spotify `spicetify apply -n`. Vesktop needs no hook because Vencord watches its files. For foot, push OSC sequences to /dev/pts because foot does not reload its config.

For Quickshell bars, write a JSON palette (the matugen quickshell.json template) and bind it through a FileView/JsonAdapter singleton with watchChanges: true, so the shell recolors instantly without a restart.

For a wallpaper picker, use either a rofi 2.0 dmenu grid (`name\0icon\x1f/path`) that calls awww and then matugen, or waypaper with `backend = awww` and `post_command = matugen image $wallpaper --source-color-index 0`. Quickshell shells (end-4 ii, DMS, caelestia) ship their own pickers. Noctalia v4 (Quickshell) is no longer maintained, so do not build on it.
deprecations_pitfalls: swww was renamed to awww in 0.12.0 and moved to Codeberg; the GitHub swww repo is now just a pointer. In nixpkgs, `swww` is a warnAlias to awww (added 2026-03-22). Binaries, the socket (${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}-awww-daemon...), env vars (AWWW_TRANSITION*) and the cache path ($XDG_CACHE_HOME/awww/<version>) all changed, so old scripts calling `swww img` break unless a compat package is installed. The Home Manager option services.swww was renamed to services.awww.

Hyprland 0.55 deprecated hyprlang (hyprland.conf) in favor of hyprland.lua, and support will be dropped after 1-2 releases. Hyprlang-style matugen templates (`$primary = rgba(...)` plus `general { col.active_border = ... }`) only suit pre-0.55 setups or hyprlock. matugen-themes' .lua template emits a table of "0xffRRGGBB" strings; whether Hyprland Lua accepts those strings as colors is unverified, and the "rgba(RRGGBBAA)" strings used in end-4's template are the proven form.
hyprpaper 0.8 dropped the `preload`/`unload` keywords and IPC requests. Use wallpaper { monitor path fit_mode } blocks and `hyprctl hyprpaper wallpaper 'mon, path, fit_mode'`.

matugen 4.0 made breaking changes: the source-color index prompt, a new default JSON shape (use `--old-json-output` for the old one), and base16 support. Unattended runs from a keybind or Quickshell can hang on the interactive picker unless --source-color-index or `prefer` is set. In config.toml, a per-template `type` needs PascalCase ("SchemeTonalSpot"), unlike the CLI's kebab-case (scheme-tonal-spot).
The matugen Nix module does NOT symlink the generated files, and it renders at build time. It cannot follow runtime wallpaper changes, so keep the CLI for runtime switching.

foot has no runtime config reload. SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2 only switch between the [colors-dark] and [colors-light] sections, and the old [colors]/[colors2] sections were removed in foot 1.28.0 after being deprecated in 1.26.0. The matugen-themes foot hook (`pkill -SIGUSR1 foot`) therefore does not load new colors into running windows.

wallust master/Codeberg HEAD is a 4.x alpha whose palette names (saliencedark, dark16, ...) and color_space key differ from the 3.5 stable release packaged in AUR and nixpkgs. Run `wallust migrate` before switching.

Stylix: the firefox target does nothing unless stylix.targets.firefox.profileNames is set. The gtk and qt targets write HM-managed files that clash with matugen writing the same paths, so disable those targets or have matugen write sibling files. Stylix has no SDDM target and no runtime theming.
catppuccin/nix no longer themes GTK widgets; the Home Manager catppuccin.gtk module only has icon options. Use adw-gtk3 plus a colors.css override instead.

Home Manager-managed dotfiles are read-only symlinks into /nix/store. If matugen's output_path points at a file Home Manager manages, writes fail or get clobbered on the next switch. Keep generated files outside HM ownership.

SDDM runs as the sddm user and reads root-owned or store themes. Runtime palette sync needs a sudoers rule (as ii-sddm-theme does) or a theme that reads colors from a world-readable path. On NixOS, prefer build-time theming such as catppuccin.sddm.
Pywalfox's dark/light mode is set inside the add-on, and 'Auto' follows time of day, not the matugen mode. Flatpak browsers and forks need a manual manifest and profile path.
Qt theming breaks when qt6ct-kde or Darkly were built against a different Qt version; rebuild the AUR packages after Qt updates. QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt6ct must be set in the session environment.

libadwaita still honors @define-color, but it is legacy (named colors survive until GTK5) and GTK_DEBUG=css prints deprecation warnings; the new API is CSS variables (--accent-bg-color, ...). GTK3 apps need the adw-gtk3 theme for the same overrides to apply.
Noctalia v4 (Quickshell-based) is no longer maintained; v5 is a native Wayland/OpenGL ES shell with no Qt. Rices built on the Quickshell Noctalia will not receive updates.
linux-wallpaperengine needs a purchased and installed Wallpaper Engine on Steam for its assets. awww, mpvpaper and linux-wallpaperengine all need wlr-layer-shell, so none of them work on GNOME.

findings.claim: Current stable NixOS is 26.05 "Yarara", released 2026-05-30. It gets updates until 2026-12-31. 25.11 "Xantusia" reached end of life on 2026-06-30.
findings.detail: On the nixos-26.05 branch, lib/.version = 26.05 and lib/trivial.nix codeName = "Yarara". The announcement says it has 7 months of support (to 2026-12-31) and that 25.11 went EOL on 2026-06-30. Headline changes: stage 1 (initrd) now runs on systemd by default, with the scripted initrd deprecated and due for removal in 26.11. The default kernel moved from 6.12 to 6.18. The Bash nixos-rebuild was removed (only the Python rewrite remains). A new /etc/nixos/system.nix entry point was added. linux_hardened and linux-rt were removed. 26.05 is the last release to support x86_64-darwin.

findings.claim: nixos-unstable is the 26.11 "Zokor" development series.
findings.detail: On nixos-unstable, lib/.version = 26.11 and codeName = "Zokor". There is no nixos-26.11 branch yet (HTTP 404). The draft rl-2611 notes remove boot.vesa and security.unprivilegedUsernsClone. The expected release month is November per the usual cadence, but I did not verify an exact date.

findings.claim: Home Manager branches: use release-26.05 with nixos-26.05, and master (which reports 26.11) with nixos-unstable.
findings.detail: release.json on master = {release: 26.11, isReleaseBranch: false}. On release-26.05 = {release: 26.05, isReleaseBranch: true}. release-25.11 still exists but is EOL. HM warns on a nixpkgs/HM version mismatch (home.enableNixpkgsReleaseCheck, default true). Standalone bootstrap: `nix run home-manager/release-26.05 -- init --switch`.

findings.claim: Package versions (checked 2026-09-25): nixos-unstable matches Arch for the desktop stack, and 26.05 is one minor version behind.
findings.detail: Hyprland: 26.05 = 0.55.4, unstable = 0.56.2, Arch extra = 0.56.2. Quickshell: 26.05 = 0.3.0, unstable = 0.3.1, Arch = 0.3.1. Matugen: 26.05 = 4.0.0, unstable = 4.2.0, Arch = 4.2.0. sddm-astronaut in nixpkgs is 0-unstable-2026-05-12 on 26.05 and 0-unstable-2026-09-18 on unstable. For raw config files shared byte-for-byte with Arch, nixos-unstable gives version parity. 26.05 risks config-API drift (Hyprland Lua API, matugen 4.0 vs 4.2).

findings.claim: Hyprland 0.55+ uses a Lua config (~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua). hyprlang (hyprland.conf) is deprecated and will be dropped after 1–2 releases.
findings.detail: From the 2026-04-26 blog post: if hyprland.lua exists it is loaded, otherwise hyprland.conf loads as before. The check happens once at startup. No new features go into hyprlang, and it will be supported for "1 - 2 releases starting from 0.55". Web search results say hyprlang is gone by 0.57, but I could not confirm that in a primary source. The Lua config can be split with require() (absolute path, relative path, or wildcard). Each require runs in its own error-protected scope. pcall(require, 'x') handles optional files. Stubs for the Lua language server are in /run/current-system/sw/share/hypr/stubs on NixOS.

findings.claim: NixOS programs.hyprland options on 26.05: enable, package, portalPackage, xwayland.enable (default true), withUWSM, systemd.setPath.enable.
findings.detail: withUWSM sets programs.uwsm.enable. The Hyprland UWSM wiki page says it produces a 'hyprland-uwsm.desktop' session entry. The module adds a cap_sys_nice security wrapper and xdg.portal with xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland, registers the session with the display manager, and links /share/hypr (Lua stubs). The enableNvidiaPatches and nvidiaPatches options were removed ('no longer needed').

findings.claim: nixpkgs Hyprland or the Hyprland flake: use nixpkgs (Hydra-cached release builds) unless you need git HEAD. The flake needs the hyprland.cachix.org substituter, and its nixpkgs input must not be overridden.
findings.detail: The wiki says to choose nixpkgs for a released version and the flake for the latest git commit. The flake is not built by Hydra, so enable Cachix before first use, and do not set inputs.hyprland.inputs.nixpkgs.follows (that makes the cache useless). On stable NixOS the flake can cause a mesa version mismatch (lag). The fix is hardware.graphics.package = hyprland's nixpkgs mesa. hyprland-plugins should use inputs.hyprland.follows = "hyprland". hyprpm is unsupported on Nix.

findings.claim: HM wayland.windowManager.hyprland on release-26.05 has a new configType option ("hyprlang" or "lua"). It defaults to "lua" when home.stateVersion >= 26.05.
findings.detail: Options: enable, package (nullable), portalPackage (nullable), plugins (list of packages or paths, loaded via `hyprctl plugin load`), configType, systemd.{enable (default true), variables, extraCommands, enableXdgAutostart}, xwayland.enable, settings, submaps, extraConfig, sourceFirst, importantPrefixes. In Lua mode each settings attribute becomes an hl.<name>(...) call. `_args` gives multi-argument calls, `_var` gives Lua locals, and lib.generators.mkLuaInline gives raw Lua. extraConfig is appended verbatim. The module writes hypr/hyprland.lua (or hyprland.conf), plus hypr/.luarc.json when a package is set. The file is generated whenever systemd.enable is true (the default), even with empty settings, so it collides with an out-of-store symlink of the whole ~/.config/hypr directory.

findings.claim: When withUWSM = true, turn off HM's Hyprland systemd integration (wayland.windowManager.hyprland.systemd.enable = false). Put env vars in ~/.config/uwsm/env and env-hyprland, not in hyprland.lua.
findings.detail: The wiki warning says HM's systemd integration conflicts with uwsm. It also advises launching apps with `uwsm app --` and using XDG autostart or systemd user units instead of exec. HM package/portalPackage can be null so the NixOS module's Hyprland is used; don't mix Hyprland and XDPH versions.

findings.claim: Quickshell: nixpkgs attr `quickshell` (0.3.0 on 26.05, 0.3.1 on unstable). The upstream flake is git+https://git.outfoxxed.me/outfoxxed/quickshell (GitHub mirror: github:quickshell-mirror/quickshell).
findings.detail: The docs say to use inputs.nixpkgs.follows (mismatched system dependencies cause crashes). The package is quickshell.packages.<system>.default. The upstream wrapper has passthru.withModules [ ... ] for extra QML modules; the nixpkgs package does not. HM has programs.quickshell {enable, package, configs, activeConfig, systemd.enable/target}; the target defaults to wayland.systemd.target = graphical-session.target, which UWSM activates. 26.05 also ships programs.dms-shell (DankMaterialShell, built on Quickshell) and services.displayManager.dms-greeter.

findings.claim: matugen is in nixpkgs (`matugen`, GPL-2.0+). The upstream flake github:InioX/matugen also provides a NixOS/HM module.
findings.detail: The README says the module does NOT symlink files automatically. Because matugen writes generated files into ~/.config paths at runtime, those target dirs must be writable. Store symlinks are read-only; out-of-store symlinks point into your git repo, so gitignore the generated outputs.

findings.claim: Stylix has release branches matching nixpkgs (release-26.05). Its default autoEnable themes most targets automatically.
findings.detail: The docs say to use stylix.url = github:nix-community/stylix/release-26.05 with NixOS 26.05. Module outputs: nixosModules.stylix and homeModules.stylix. stylix.autoEnable = false disables all targets unless explicitly enabled. That matters if matugen and raw dotfiles are your theming source of truth, since Stylix would otherwise generate competing configs.

findings.claim: NVIDIA on 26.05: the default 'stable' branch resolves to production 595.71.05. hardware.nvidia.open must be set explicitly (assertion for drivers >= 560). New options: hardware.nvidia.branch and hardware.nvidia.moduleParams.
findings.detail: The open default is null for drivers >= 560, with the assertion message "You must configure `hardware.nvidia.open` on NVIDIA driver versions >= 560". Use open modules on Turing or newer (RTX, GTX 16xx). modesetting.enable defaults true for >= 535 (framebuffer device on >= 545). videoAcceleration (nvidia-vaapi-driver) defaults to true. powerManagement.kernelSuspendNotifier defaults on for open modules >= 595. Branches: stable, production (595.71.05), new_feature (590.48.01), beta (595.45.04), latest, bleeding_edge, legacy_580/535/470/390/340. moduleParams now go to modprobe config instead of the kernel command line. EGL platform libraries are built from source. The module is enabled by services.xserver.videoDrivers = ["nvidia"]. PRIME options: prime.offload.enable, prime.offload.enableOffloadCmd (nvidia-offload script), prime.sync.enable, prime.reverseSync.enable, plus intelBusId/amdgpuBusId/nvidiaBusId. Bus IDs are decimal and accept both 'PCI:1:0:0' and 'PCI:1@0:0:0'. powerManagement.finegrained is for offload (RTD3).

findings.claim: Hyprland on NVIDIA: the wiki says to set LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia and __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia, and NVD_BACKEND=direct for VA-API. On NixOS, set NIXOS_OZONE_WL=1 for Electron apps.
findings.detail: The wiki notes modeset is already on by default on NixOS for drivers after 535. With UWSM, put these vars in ~/.config/uwsm/env instead of hyprland.lua.

findings.claim: chaotic-nyx was archived on 2025-12-08 and has since come back: the repo is not archived and was committing daily as of 2026-09-25.
findings.detail: A Discourse thread (Feb 2026) says Nyx was archived on 2025-12-08 and that xddxdd/nix-cachyos-kernel became the main way to get CachyOS kernels. The chaotic-cx/nyx README now says "WE'RE BACK FROM THE DEAD!" and the GitHub commit list shows automated bumps dated 2026-09-25. Its full modules are for nixos-unstable only. On the latest stable you use nyx-cache, nyx-overlay and nyx-registry, with pkgs.linuxPackages_cachyos (variants: lts, rc, server, hardened, lto-znver4, gcc; claims kconfig parity with CachyOS). A CachyOS kernel is NOT in nixpkgs; the Feb 2026 proposal met objections (build load, LTO incompatibility). Alternative: github:xddxdd/nix-cachyos-kernel/release with overlays.pinned and pkgs.cachyosKernels.linuxPackages-cachyos-latest (and -lts, -bore, -lto, x86_64-v3/v4, zen4 variants). Its Attic cache is https://attic.xuyh0120.win/lantian (key lantian:EeAUQ+W+6r7EtwnmYjeVwx5kOGEBpjlBfPlzGlTNvHc=). Do not override its nixpkgs input.

findings.claim: Flake structure: a plain flake with a small mkHost helper is enough for a few hosts. flake-parts helps when you want outputs split into modules (perSystem, devShells, formatter, pre-commit).
findings.detail: flake-parts describes itself as a minimal mirror of the flake schema built on the module system; you migrate by wrapping outputs in flake-parts.lib.mkFlake { inherit inputs; } { systems = [...]; flake = {...}; }. fufexan's Hyprland-maintainer dotfiles use flake-parts with ./hosts ./lib ./modules ./pkgs, and pass specialArgs = { inherit inputs self; } plus home-manager.extraSpecialArgs = specialArgs and backupFileExtension. Misterio77's starter configs use a plain flake with overlays/default.nix (additions, modifications, unstable-packages). HM docs: pass flake inputs with home-manager.extraSpecialArgs = { inherit inputs; } and prefer that over _module.args. nixpkgs' flake notes that nixosSystem's `system` argument is a legacy alias for nixpkgs.hostPlatform, which hardware-configuration.nix already sets.

findings.claim: HM NixOS-module settings to use: useGlobalPkgs, useUserPackages, extraSpecialArgs, sharedModules, backupFileExtension, backupCommand, overwriteBackup.
findings.detail: useGlobalPkgs makes HM use the system pkgs, so overlays and allowUnfree are set once at NixOS level and HM's nixpkgs.* options are disabled. backupFileExtension moves colliding unmanaged files aside. overwriteBackup (new) lets it clobber an existing backup.

findings.claim: config.lib.file.mkOutOfStoreSymlink makes live-editable links, but in a flake you must pass an absolute STRING path. A ./relative path resolves into the flake's /nix/store copy.
findings.detail: mkOutOfStoreSymlink is `pkgs.runCommandLocal name {} "ln -s ${toString path} $out"`. With flakes the source tree is copied to the store first, so ./foo becomes /nix/store/...-source/foo (HM issues #2085 and #2660; builtins.toString doesn't help). Use "${config.home.homeDirectory}/dotfiles/...". With the default recursive = false, the target is a single symlink to the directory.

findings.claim: Recommended way to share the SAME raw dotfiles between Arch and NixOS: one repo with a plain config/<app>/ tree as the source of truth. Arch links it with GNU Stow (or chezmoi in symlink mode). NixOS links the same directories with HM xdg.configFile.<app>.source = mkOutOfStoreSymlink "<abs path>". HM handles packages, services and system glue, not app configs.
findings.detail: Both OSes end up with ~/.config/<app> as a symlink into the git checkout, so edits apply instantly with no rebuild ("Same behavior as stow" — Matt Michie, 2026). Pros: one source of truth; editing and hot reload (Hyprland reloads on file change; quickshell live-reloads) work the same on both OSes; no Nix language needed for app configs; Arch needs no Nix at all. Cons: not reproducible or pure (the flake doesn't capture the files, and a broken edit isn't caught at build time); the repo path is hard-coded; you lose HM's typed program modules for these apps and must not enable them for the same files (they collide: 'Conflicting managed target files' or 'Existing file ... is in the way'); runtime-written files (matugen output, app state) land in the repo and need .gitignore; per-host differences must be handled inside the config (Hyprland Lua `pcall(require, 'host')`, uwsm env files) or with HM-generated files outside the linked dirs. Alternatives: (a) run stow or chezmoi on NixOS too and skip HM for dotfiles — simplest, identical on both; (b) Hjem, a lighter HM alternative featured on the Hyprland wiki, which now has a standalone CLI for non-NixOS.

findings.claim: HM standalone on Arch works (targets.genericLinux.enable), but running the graphical/session stack from Nix on Arch has sharp edges. Install Hyprland, quickshell, lockers, greeter and drivers with pacman, and use HM on Arch only for CLI tools, or not at all.
findings.detail: targets.genericLinux.enable adds Nix profile XDG_DATA_DIRS and XCURSOR_PATH and sources nix.sh. It also auto-enables targets.genericLinux.gpu, which needs a one-time `sudo /nix/store/...-non-nixos-gpu/bin/non-nixos-gpu-setup` to install a tmpfiles.d link to /run/opengl-driver. Proprietary NVIDIA needs gpu.nvidia.version and sha256 matching the host driver EXACTLY, so every Arch nvidia update means a Nix config bump. PAM is broken for Nix-built lockers on non-NixOS: pam_unix calls /run/wrappers/bin/unix_chkpwd (HM issue #7027; nixpkgs #128523). HM's advice is to set the locker package to null and use the distro's build, which also affects Quickshell lockscreens. Hyprland from Nix on another distro needs nixGL (start-hyprland auto-uses it since 0.53.2) and a manual symlink of the wayland-sessions .desktop into /usr/share. Arch wiki: install `nix`, enable nix-daemon; Arch extra ships nix 2.35.2.

findings.claim: Secrets: sops-nix and agenix are both current. sops-nix adds templates, placeholders and YAML/JSON multi-key files. agenix is simpler, with one .age file per secret.
findings.detail: sops-nix: inputs.sops-nix.url = github:Mic92/sops-nix; module sops-nix.nixosModules.sops; HM module homeManagerModules.sops (usable via home-manager.sharedModules); sops.templates."x".content with config.sops.placeholder.<name>. agenix: github:ryantm/agenix; agenix.nixosModules.default; agenix.homeManagerModules.default; age.secrets.<n>.file and .path (/run/agenix/<n>). New in 26.05: services.openssh.generateHostKeys = true creates host keys without running sshd, useful for either tool.

findings.claim: Lanzaboote: pin the v1.1.0 tag. Replace systemd-boot with boot.lanzaboote and pkiBundle = "/var/lib/sbctl". Alternatively, nixpkgs' Limine module supports Secure Boot via sbctl.
findings.detail: Steps: `sudo sbctl create-keys`, rebuild, `sudo sbctl verify` (files starting with kernel- are expected to be unsigned), then enable Secure Boot in firmware. Limine options on 26.05: boot.loader.limine.{enable, efiSupport, secureBoot.{enable, autoGenerateKeys, autoEnrollKeys}, style.{wallpapers, wallpaperStyle, backdrop, interface.*, graphicalTerminal.*}}. That makes Limine a themable bootloader with Secure Boot.

findings.claim: Boot theming: systemd-boot has essentially no theming (only consoleMode, timeout, etc.). Use GRUB's boot.loader.grub.theme (a path; e.g. pkgs.catppuccin-grub, pkgs.sleek-grub-theme, pkgs.minimal-grub-theme) or Limine's style.*. Plymouth handles the themed splash.
findings.detail: catppuccin-grub installs the chosen flavour's theme files at $out (override { flavor = "mocha"; }). Plymouth per the NixOS wiki: boot.plymouth.{enable, theme, themePackages = [ (adi1090x-plymouth-themes.override { selected_themes = ["rings"]; }) ]}. Silent boot uses consoleLogLevel = 3, initrd.verbose = false, kernelParams ["quiet" "rd.udev.log_level=3" "rd.systemd.show_status=auto"] and loader.timeout = 0. Without selected_themes, adi1090x installs every theme (~524M). Since 26.05 uses systemd in the initrd by default, these rd.systemd params apply.

findings.claim: Greeters: greetd with tuigreet (pkgs.tuigreet 0.11.1, now at github.com/tuigreet/tuigreet), or SDDM with pkgs.sddm-astronaut (Qt6, uses kdePackages.sddm).
findings.detail: The greetd module has a new useTextGreeter option that stops boot messages from spamming the TUI, and it creates /var/cache/tuigreet for --remember*. default_session.user defaults to "greeter". List sessions with config.services.displayManager.sessionData.desktops. SDDM: services.displayManager.sddm.{enable, package (default kdePackages.sddm), theme, extraPackages, wayland.enable, settings}. sddm-astronaut supports override { embeddedTheme = "japanese_aesthetic"; themeConfig = {...}; }. Set theme = "sddm-astronaut-theme" and add kdePackages.qtmultimedia to extraPackages for video backgrounds. 26.05 also added the dms-greeter module (greetd-based) for DankMaterialShell.

findings.claim: Audio, Bluetooth and power: services.pipewire (wireplumber is on by default), services.pulseaudio.enable = false, hardware.bluetooth (powerOnBoot defaults to true), services.blueman. Use power-profiles-daemon or tuned, not both.
findings.detail: hardware.pulseaudio was renamed to services.pulseaudio, and PipeWire asserts that PulseAudio is off. services.tuned asserts it conflicts with services.power-profiles-daemon, services.tlp, services.auto-cpufreq and hardware.system76.power-daemon. tuned provides a PPD-compatible API by default (ppdSupport = true), so desktop shells expecting PPD keep working. tuned also requires security.polkit.

findings.claim: Nerd Fonts are per-font attributes under pkgs.nerd-fonts.<name>. The old pkgs.nerdfonts alias is gone from 26.05 aliases.nix.
findings.detail: Attribute names are the lowercase caskName, with a leading '_' if it starts with a digit. Examples: jetbrains-mono, fira-code, symbols-only, caskaydia-cove, iosevka, meslo-lg, hack, ubuntu-mono, geist-mono, commit-mono, _0xproto, _3270. noto-fonts-emoji is a throw alias; use noto-fonts-color-emoji. 26.05 sets fonts.fontconfig.useEmbeddedBitmaps = true by default.

findings.claim: Tooling: nh 4.4.2 is in nixpkgs, with NixOS programs.nh {flake, clean.{enable, dates, extraArgs}} and HM programs.nh {flake, osFlake, homeFlake}. nix-index-database provides nixosModules.default and homeModules.default. nix-ld is programs.nix-ld {enable, libraries}.
findings.detail: nh: `nh os switch` or `nh home switch . -c <name>`; NH_FLAKE / NH_OS_FLAKE let you omit the path; `nh clean all` handles garbage collection. nix-index-database: don't also install nix-index in systemPackages; set programs.nix-index-database.comma.enable = true for comma. nix-ld: the libraries default is a base set, extend as needed.

findings.claim: disko, impermanence and nixos-hardware follow the usual flake input and module pattern.
findings.detail: disko: run `sudo nix --experimental-features "nix-command flakes" run github:nix-community/disko/latest -- --mode destroy,format,mount disk-config.nix`, or use disko-install. The btrfs subvolume example includes /rootfs, /home, /nix and a swap subvolume. impermanence: impermanence.nixosModules.impermanence with environment.persistence."/persistent" = { hideMounts; directories; files; users.<u>.directories }; you can set inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "" and inputs.home-manager.follows = "" to trim the lock file. 26.05 notes that esphome moved to a static user, so persist /var/lib/esphome. nixos-hardware: nixos-hardware.nixosModules.<model>, with common modules such as common-cpu-amd-pstate, common-gpu-nvidia, common-gpu-nvidia-nonprime, common-pc-laptop, common-pc-ssd. Its README now shows inputs.nixpkgs.follows.

findings.claim: The NixOS versions of some packages differ from Arch's in how they are laid out, so raw configs must avoid FHS paths.
findings.detail: The NixOS store has no /usr/lib or /usr/share. Raw configs that hard-code /usr/bin/..., /usr/lib/polkit-..., or /usr/share/... paths break on NixOS. Call binaries by name through PATH, and start helpers as systemd user units (hyprpolkitagent is in nixpkgs, and HM has services.hyprpolkitagent). Matt Michie's migration hit the same kind of problem (hard-coded /opt/homebrew paths).
