recommendations: Base the NixOS hosts on nixos-unstable with HM master. As of 2026-09-25 it matches Arch exactly for Hyprland 0.56.2, quickshell 0.3.1 and matugen 4.2.0, so raw configs behave identically. If you want 26.05 stability, use HM release-26.05 and stylix/release-26.05, and expect Hyprland 0.55.4 and matugen 4.0.0 there.

Make config/<app>/ in the repo the single source of truth for app configs (hypr, quickshell, matugen, kitty, uwsm, ...). On Arch run `stow -d ~/dotfiles -t ~/.config config`. On NixOS use an HM module that maps each app to xdg.configFile.<app>.source = config.lib.file.mkOutOfStoreSymlink "${config.home.homeDirectory}/dotfiles/config/<app>" (absolute string only). Use HM only for packages, services, cursor/GTK glue and per-host generated files outside the linked dirs.

Do not enable HM modules that generate files for apps whose directories you link raw. In particular wayland.windowManager.hyprland writes hypr/hyprland.lua whenever systemd.enable is true, and hypr/.luarc.json. Enable Hyprland at system level with programs.hyprland.enable + withUWSM = true.

Write the shared Hyprland config in Lua (hyprland.lua), since hyprlang is deprecated. Split it with require(), load optional per-host files with pcall(require, 'host'), put env vars in ~/.config/uwsm/env and env-hyprland, start apps with `uwsm app --`, and never hard-code /usr/... paths.

On Arch, install the whole graphical stack (Hyprland, quickshell, SDDM or greetd, hyprlock, pipewire, NVIDIA) with pacman/AUR. Use HM standalone only for CLI tools if you want it; stow alone is enough for the dotfiles. Nix-built lockers can't use PAM on non-NixOS, Nix GL needs a sudo setup step, and the Nix NVIDIA libraries must be re-pinned to the host driver version on every Arch driver update.

Use a plain flake with a mkHost helper (specialArgs plus home-manager.extraSpecialArgs = { inherit inputs self hostname user; }, useGlobalPkgs = true, backupFileExtension). Move to flake-parts only if you want perSystem devShells, formatter or pre-commit and outputs split across files.

On NVIDIA hosts set hardware.nvidia.open explicitly (true for Turing and newer), keep modesetting on, set services.xserver.videoDrivers = ["nvidia"] even on pure Wayland, and put LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME, __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME and NVD_BACKEND in the uwsm env file for those hosts.

For a themed boot: Plymouth (adi1090x with selected_themes) plus silent kernel params, and either GRUB with pkgs.catppuccin-grub or Limine with style.* (Limine also covers Secure Boot). systemd-boot is fine if you don't need a themed menu; use Lanzaboote v1.1.0 for Secure Boot with it.
For the login screen, pick SDDM + sddm-astronaut for a themed Qt6 greeter, or greetd + tuigreet with useTextGreeter = true for a minimal one. Both list the 'Hyprland (uwsm-managed)' session.

For a CachyOS kernel on NixOS, prefer xddxdd/nix-cachyos-kernel/release with overlays.pinned and its Attic cache. chaotic-nyx is active again and works too; its full modules are unstable-only. Configure the cache and rebuild before switching kernels.

Use sops-nix if you need templated config files or HM secrets; agenix is enough for simple per-file secrets. Add impermanence and disko only if you want a reinstallable, ephemeral-root setup. They are optional for a first NixOS host.

Skip Stylix, or set stylix.autoEnable = false, when matugen plus raw dotfiles is your theming pipeline; otherwise the two fight over the same configs. Gitignore matugen's generated outputs inside the linked dirs.
deprecations_pitfalls: hardware.nvidia.open has no default for drivers >= 560, and evaluation fails with an assertion until you set it.
26.05 uses systemd in the initrd by default and deprecates the scripted stage 1 (removal planned in 26.11). With LUKS, set fileSystems."/".device = "/dev/mapper/<name>". /dev/root no longer exists.
The Bash nixos-rebuild was removed in 26.05, and system.rebuild.enableNg must be removed from configs.

hardware.pulseaudio became services.pulseaudio, and hardware.opengl.* became hardware.graphics.*. The pkgs.nerdfonts alias is gone (use nerd-fonts.<name>), and noto-fonts-emoji throws (use noto-fonts-color-emoji).
linux_hardened and linux-rt kernels were removed in 26.05. 26.05 is the last release with x86_64-darwin.

Hyprland: hyprlang (.conf) is deprecated since 0.55 and slated for removal. HM's configType defaults to "lua" for stateVersion >= 26.05. A hyprland.lua, if present, always wins over hyprland.conf, and the check only happens at startup.
programs.hyprland.enableNvidiaPatches and nvidiaPatches were removed. hyprpm does not work on Nix; use wayland.windowManager.hyprland.plugins.
Overriding the Hyprland flake's nixpkgs input makes Cachix useless. Using the flake on stable NixOS can cause a mesa mismatch.
HM's Hyprland systemd integration conflicts with UWSM; set systemd.enable = false or don't use the HM module.

mkOutOfStoreSymlink with a ./relative path inside a flake points into /nix/store (HM #2085/#2660); only absolute strings work. Linked dirs are live repo dirs, so apps and matugen write into your git tree.

HM refuses to overwrite existing files ('Existing file ... is in the way'). Use home-manager.backupFileExtension (NixOS module) or `home-manager switch -b backup`. Two HM entries targeting the same path fail with 'Conflicting managed target files'.

HM on non-NixOS: PAM-based lockers built by Nix fail (unix_chkpwd path, HM #7027). GPU needs non-nixos-gpu-setup via sudo, and NVIDIA needs an exact driver version and hash. Nix Hyprland on another distro needs nixGL and a manual wayland-sessions symlink.
services.tuned cannot coexist with power-profiles-daemon, TLP or auto-cpufreq (assertion).
adi1090x-plymouth-themes without selected_themes pulls every theme (~524M).
chaotic-nyx was archived on 2025-12-08 and later revived. Older guides call it dead, and newer ones point to xddxdd/nix-cachyos-kernel. There is no CachyOS kernel in nixpkgs.
nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem's `system` argument is a legacy alias. hardware-configuration.nix already sets nixpkgs.hostPlatform.

Stylix, the Hyprland flake and chaotic's full modules all assume matching branches (release-26.05 with 26.05, master with unstable). Mixing branches produces HM/nixpkgs mismatch warnings or build errors.
Unverified: an exact 26.11 release date, and the claim that Hyprland 0.57 fully removes hyprlang (came from web search, not a primary source).

findings.claim: archinstall's current release is 4.4. It was tagged on 2026-06-28 and is the version in Arch [extra] and on PyPI.
findings.detail: archinstall 4.4 is in [extra] (last_update 2026-06-28). pyproject.toml at tag 4.4 says version = "4.4". Earlier tags: 4.3 (2026-04-20) and 4.2 (2026-04-15). Git tags have no 'v' prefix, so raw URLs use /4.4/ and /v4.4/ returns 404. The JSON format below comes from reading the parsers at the 4.4 tag. The docs example in docs/installing/guided.rst is out of date: it uses 'length' where the parser reads partition['size'].

findings.claim: archinstall 4.4 command-line flags for unattended installs
findings.detail: --config <file> or --config-url <url> (main JSON). --creds <file> or --creds-url <url> (credentials JSON). --creds-decryption-key, or the env var ARCHINSTALL_CREDS_DECRYPTION_KEY, for an encrypted creds file. --silent turns off every prompt but is ignored when no config is given. --dry-run ('Generates a configuration file and then exits'). Also --mountpoint (default /mnt), --skip-ntp, --skip-wkd, --skip-boot, --offline, --no-pkg-lookups, --plugin/--plugin-url, --skip-version-check, --skip-wifi-check, --advanced, --debug. --debug writes credentials into the log. Default output filenames are user_configuration.json and user_credentials.json.

findings.claim: Top-level keys archinstall 4.4 reads from the config file, and which old keys still work
findings.detail: Current keys: script, archinstall-language, locale_config{kb_layout,sys_lang,sys_enc,console_font}, disk_config, profile_config, mirror_config{mirror_regions,custom_servers,optional_repositories,custom_repositories}, network_config{type: iso|nm|nm_iwd|iwd|manual, nics[] when manual}, bootloader_config, app_config, auth_config{u2f_config}, hostname, kernels[], ntp, packages[], pacman_config{parallel_downloads,color}, swap{enabled, algorithm: zstd|lzo-rle|lzo|lz4|lz4hc} (zram), timezone, services[], custom_commands[]. Old keys still accepted: top-level audio_config, bootloader + uki, disk_encryption, parallel_downloads, additional-repositories, !root-password, !users. optional_repositories values: multilib, testing, core-testing, extra-testing, multilib-testing.

findings.claim: bootloader_config supports Limine, GRUB, systemd-boot, EFISTUB and rEFInd, plus an optional Plymouth theme
findings.detail: bootloader must be one of: 'No bootloader', 'Systemd-boot', 'Grub', 'Efistub', 'Limine', 'Refind'. Matching is case-insensitive via capitalize(). The other keys are uki (bool), removable (bool; only GRUB and Limine support it) and an optional plymouth theme: bgrt, fade-in, glow, script, solar, spinner, spinfinity, tribar, text or details. Systemd-boot, Efistub and Refind work on UEFI only. Defaults are systemd-boot on UEFI and GRUB on BIOS.

findings.claim: disk_config schema, with btrfs subvolumes and compression
findings.detail: config_type is default_layout, manual_partitioning or pre_mounted_config (the last one needs 'mountpoint'). device_modifications is a list of {device, wipe, partitions[]}. Each partition has: obj_id (any string), status (create/existing/modify/delete), type (primary/boot), start and size as {value, unit (B, KiB, MiB, GiB, sectors...), sector_size {value, unit}}, fs_type (btrfs, ext4, xfs, f2fs, fat32, ntfs, linux-swap...), mountpoint (null for a btrfs partition that uses subvolumes), mount_options[], flags[] (boot, esp, bls_boot, linux-home, swap), dev_path, and btrfs [{name, mountpoint}]. The parser checks that: the first partition starts at 1 MiB or later; partitions do not overlap; start and size are MiB-aligned; and on GPT the last partition ends at least 1 MiB before the end of the disk. Size values therefore depend on the specific disk. Compression is set with mount_options ["compress=zstd"], which also makes archinstall run 'chattr +c' on each subvolume. The TUI's other btrfs option is 'nodatacow'. The default subvolumes are @ (/), @home, @log (/var/log) and @pkg (/var/cache/pacman/pkg). There is no @snapshots. disk_encryption (luks, lvm_on_luks, luks_on_lvm) now goes inside disk_config.

findings.claim: archinstall's built-in Snapper support is GRUB-only and uses snapper's default nested .snapshots, not the wiki's flat @snapshots layout
findings.detail: This is disk_config.btrfs_options.snapshot_config.type = Snapper or Timeshift. It only runs if some subvolume is mounted at '/'. It installs snapper, runs 'snapper --no-dbus -c root create-config /' and '-c home create-config /home', and enables snapper-timeline.timer and snapper-cleanup.timer. When the bootloader is Grub it also installs grub-btrfs and inotify-tools and enables grub-btrfsd with ExecStart=/usr/bin/grub-btrfsd --syslog /.snapshots. There is no Limine or limine-snapper-sync support. If you define your own @snapshots subvolume mounted at /.snapshots, leave snapshot_config unset and set up snapper yourself. The wiki procedure requires that /.snapshots does not exist before create-config, so archinstall's create-config would probably fail in that case.

findings.claim: When archinstall installs Limine, its limine.conf hides the $ESP/limine.conf that limine-snapper-sync and limine-entry-tool manage
findings.detail: On UEFI, archinstall copies BOOTX64.EFI to ESP/EFI/arch-limine/ (or EFI/BOOT/ when removable) and writes limine.conf in the same folder. Entries use boot():/vmlinuz-<kernel> and cmdline with rootflags=subvol=@. It also adds a 99-limine.hook pacman hook. Limine searches for the config in this order: <EFI app path>/limine.conf first, then /boot/limine/limine.conf, /boot/limine.conf, /limine/limine.conf, /limine.conf. limine-entry-tool and limine-snapper-sync only write $ESP_PATH/limine.conf and say to 'remove any alternative Limine config files'. Keep the ESP mounted at /boot: snapshot entries need the kernels on the same ESP as limine.conf.

findings.claim: archinstall sets up a systemd-based initramfs by default, which decides which btrfs-overlayfs hook you can use
findings.detail: Default HOOKS are base systemd autodetect microcode modconf kms keyboard sd-vconsole block filesystems fsck. They switch to udev/keymap/encrypt only for LUKS without a FIDO2 device. So for Limine snapshots use sd-btrfs-overlayfs (from limine-mkinitcpio-hook). grub-btrfs-overlayfs is a busybox-only runtime hook and does not work with a systemd initramfs.

findings.claim: custom_commands run as root in the chroot before genfstab
findings.detail: Each command is written to /var/tmp/user-command.N.sh on the target and run with 'arch-chroot -S <target> bash <script>'. This happens after users, the profile, services and the snapshot setup, but before genfstab. They run as root, so makepkg and AUR helpers won't work there. Keep AUR work and the ricing for a stage that runs as your user after first boot.

findings.claim: archinstall's Hyprland profile, greeters and graphics driver values
findings.detail: Use profile_config.profile {main: 'Desktop', details: ['Hyprland'], custom_settings: {Hyprland: {seat_access: 'polkit'|'seatd'}}}. It installs hyprland, dunst, kitty, uwsm, dolphin, wofi, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland, qt5-wayland, qt6-wayland, polkit-kde-agent, grim and slurp, with SDDM as the default greeter. Greeter options: sddm, gdm, ly, lightdm-gtk-greeter, lightdm-slick-greeter, cosmic-greeter, plasma-login-manager, dms-greeter. gfx_driver options: 'All open-source', 'AMD / ATI (open-source)', 'Intel (open-source)', 'Nvidia (open kernel module for newer GPUs, Turing+)', 'Nvidia (open-source nouveau driver)', 'VirtualBox (open-source)'. 'Nvidia (proprietary)' now fails with an error saying nvidia-dkms was removed. app_config takes audio_config.audio (pipewire|pulseaudio|'No audio server'), bluetooth_config.enabled, power_management_config.power_management (power-profiles-daemon|tuned), print_service_config.enabled, firewall_config.firewall (ufw|firewalld) and fonts_config.fonts (noto-fonts, noto-fonts-emoji, noto-fonts-cjk, ttf-liberation, ttf-dejavu).

findings.claim: Credentials (--creds) format
findings.detail: users: [{username, enc_password (crypt hash; archinstall generates yescrypt) or '!password' (plaintext), sudo (bool), groups []}], plus root_enc_password and encryption_password (the LUKS passphrase). archinstall can encrypt the creds file when saving (Fernet), and --creds-decryption-key decrypts it. The most reliable way to get valid hashes is to run 'archinstall --dry-run' once and save the creds it produces.

findings.claim: Almost the whole Hyprland stack is in official [extra]. AUR is only needed for a few theming and app packages.
findings.detail: In [extra]: hyprland 0.56.2, hyprlock 0.9.6, hypridle 0.1.8, hyprpaper 0.8.4, hyprsunset 0.4.0, hyprpolkitagent 0.1.3, hyprpicker 0.4.7, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland 1.4.1, uwsm 0.27.0, quickshell 0.3.1, matugen 4.2.0, awww 0.12.1, waybar 0.15.0, swaync 0.12.6, rofi 2.0.0, fuzzel 1.15.0, cliphist 0.7.0, wl-clipboard 2.3.0, hyprshot 1.3.0, satty 0.22.0, swappy 1.8.0, kitty 0.48.2, ghostty 1.3.1, fastfetch 2.68.1, starship 1.26.0, eza 0.23.5, bat 0.26.1, zoxide 0.10.0, fzf 0.74.4, yazi 26.9.1, btop 1.4.7, cava 1.0.0, nwg-look 1.1.1, qt6ct 0.11, kvantum 1.1.8, papirus-icon-theme 20260801, ttf-jetbrains-mono-nerd 3.5.1, sddm 0.21.0, plymouth 26.134.222, snapper 0.13.2, btrfs-assistant 2.3.1, grub-btrfs 4.14, limine 12.9.0, snap-pac 3.0.1, stow, chezmoi, yadm, gum 2.0.1, libnewt (whiptail), dms-shell 1.6.2 (+ dms-shell-hyprland). AUR only: bibata-cursor-theme(-bin), maplemono-* (split package base 'maplemono', 7.9), sddm-astronaut-theme, spicetify-cli, python-pywalfox, vesktop / vesktop-bin, limine-snapper-sync, limine-mkinitcpio-hook, grimblast-git (there is no plain 'grimblast'), wallust, wlogout, paru, yay. Not found in either the official repos or the AUR under those names: swww, rofi-wayland, ttf-maple, hyprland-qtutils.

findings.claim: Renames and removals that break older scripts
findings.detail: swww is replaced by awww: [extra] awww has provides/replaces=swww but ships only /usr/bin/awww and /usr/bin/awww-daemon, with no swww binary. nixpkgs also aliases swww to awww as of 2026-03-22. rofi-wayland is replaced by rofi 2.0.0 (provides/replaces rofi-wayland; native Wayland). hyprland-qtutils is replaced by hyprland-guiutils (a hyprland dependency). nvidia/nvidia-dkms were replaced by nvidia-open/nvidia-open-dkms on 2025-12-20 (driver 590 dropped Pascal and older). GTX 10xx and older cards need nvidia-580xx-dkms from the AUR. Also, the hyprland 0.56.2 package now depends on lua and ships both hyprland.desktop and hyprland-uwsm.desktop sessions.

findings.claim: The AUR had large malware incidents in 2025–2026, so an unattended script should keep its AUR list short and reviewed
findings.detail: July 2025: the CHAOS RAT was found in librewolf-fix-bin, firefox-patch-bin and zen-browser-patched-bin. 2026-06-12: Arch news 'Active AUR malicious packages incident' reported malicious adoptions and updates and told users to review every PKGBUILD and install-script change. Press coverage puts that wave at about 1,579 packages. About 2026-07-31, AUR package adoptions were disabled after another wave. The Arch Wiki warns that AUR PKGBUILDs are 'completely unofficial and have not been thoroughly vetted'. It mentions traur and ks-aur-scanner as scanning aids, not replacements for reading the files.

findings.claim: paru vs yay: both are capable; yay is the more active project in 2026, and paru-bin is orphaned
findings.detail: yay 13.0.1 (AUR yay and yay-bin, both maintained by upstream author jguer; 2653 votes) was released 2026-06-19. v13.0.0 (2026-06-17) added Lua configuration and the hooks AURPreInstall, UpgradeSelect and AURPostDownload. paru's last release is v2.1.0 (2025-07-08). The AUR 'paru' package is maintained by upstream Morganamilo (1256 votes, rebuilt 2025-12-12). 'paru-bin' has no maintainer and has been flagged out of date since 2025-12-13. The Arch Wiki comparison lists both with file review, diff view, reliable parser, reliable solver and batch operations. paru also builds in a clean chroot and can use a local repository. Chaotic-AUR ships prebuilt paru and yay.

findings.claim: How to enable Chaotic-AUR, and what it covers
findings.detail: Import and lsign key 3056513887B78AEB. Install chaotic-keyring and chaotic-mirrorlist from cdn-mirror.chaotic.cx. Append [chaotic-aur] with Include=/etc/pacman.d/chaotic-mirrorlist at the END of pacman.conf. Most packages are built automatically from their AUR sources. Inference: this means a malicious AUR update would probably also appear as a prebuilt binary without human review. As of 2026-09-25 it has bibata-cursor-theme, grimblast-git, limine-mkinitcpio-hook, limine-snapper-sync, sddm-astronaut-theme (75.c10bd95, newer than the stale AUR 62.x), spicetify-cli, vesktop, paru, yay, hyprshell, linux-cachyos(-bore,-lts,-rc) and nvidia-580xx-dkms. It does not have python-pywalfox, maplemono or wallust (only wallust-git).

findings.claim: Adding CachyOS repos to vanilla Arch replaces pacman and puts CachyOS repos above [core]
findings.detail: The official method is curl https://mirror.cachyos.org/cachyos-repo.tar.xz, extract it, then run 'sudo ./cachyos-repo.sh'. The script: imports key F3B607488DB35A47; runs 'pacman -U' on cachyos-keyring, the mirrorlists and CachyOS's own pacman build (pacman-7.1.0.r9.g54d9411-4); detects znver4/5 (gcc -march=native), x86-64-v4 or x86-64-v3; backs up /etc/pacman.conf to /etc/pacman.conf.bak; inserts [cachyos-v3]/[cachyos-core-v3]/[cachyos-extra-v3]/[cachyos] (or the v4/znver4 variants) BEFORE [core] and sets Architecture = auto; then runs pacman -Syu. Result: many Arch packages are replaced by CachyOS rebuilds, so the system becomes a partial CachyOS. '--remove' runs pacman -Suuy, reinstalls core/pacman, and reinstalls every native package with 'pacman -Qqn | pacman -S -'. The wiki warns that Intel 12th gen and newer can report x86-64-v4 but can't actually run AVX-512. CachyOS's pacman fork adds features such as INSTALLED_FROM. Kernel variants: linux-cachyos (Clang+ThinLTO+AutoFDO), -bore, -eevdf, -lts, -hardened, -rc, -server, -rt-bore, -bmq, -deckify.

findings.claim: Recommended snapshot layout: flat @snapshots, with snapper plus limine-snapper-sync (for Limine) or grub-btrfs (for GRUB)
findings.detail: The Arch Wiki suggests @ (/), @home, @snapshots (/.snapshots) and @var_log as a flat layout, and recommends separate subvolumes for /var/cache, /var/tmp, docker and so on. /var/lib/pacman must stay in @. The procedure: umount and rm /.snapshots, run create-config, delete the nested .snapshots subvolume, mkdir /.snapshots, mount @snapshots via fstab, chmod 750. limine-snapper-sync (AUR, by Zesko): boots Snapper snapshots from the Limine menu; restores with rsync, replace or native snapper; auto-repairs boot files; needs Limine 8 or newer, a FAT32 ESP of about 4 GiB or more (NVIDIA DKMS can take over 300 MiB per kernel), /usr/lib/modules inside the root subvolume, the '//Snapshots' keyword in $ESP/limine.conf, and snapshots taken after it was installed. Read-only snapshots need overlayfs (sd-btrfs-overlayfs with systemd hooks). snap-pac takes pre/post snapshots around pacman transactions. grub-btrfsd plus inotify-tools adds GRUB menu entries, and archinstall can set that up automatically.

findings.claim: For a dotfiles repo shared with NixOS, GNU Stow on Arch plus Home Manager's mkOutOfStoreSymlink on NixOS is the simplest fit
findings.detail: Both approaches symlink into the same plain-file working tree, so an edit shows up on both systems without rebuilding. chezmoi (Go, single binary) creates real files and stores its source under special names (dot_, private_, executable_, .tmpl). It has templates, encryption and password-manager integration, but Home Manager can't read that source layout directly, and both tools would try to own the same targets. yadm (a bare-repo-style Bash script) uses alternate files and templates in $HOME. dotbot (Python+git, installed as a git submodule, config file required) creates symlinks. Stow 2.4.1 is in [extra] and offers --no-folding, --dotfiles, -n/--simulate and --adopt (--adopt changes your repo). mkOutOfStoreSymlink must get an absolute string path: with flakes, a relative ./path is copied into the store (home-manager issues #2660 and #2085).

findings.claim: The JaKooLit Arch-Hyprland and Hyprland-Dots projects moved to LinuxBeginnings in March 2026
findings.detail: Both READMEs say: 'Beginning of March 2026, This project will be archived and it will be maintained by Dwilliams' (github.com/LinuxBeginnings). JaKooLit/Arch-Hyprland's last commit is 2026-02-22. LinuxBeginnings/Arch-Hyprland is active (commit on 2026-09-24) and has updated package names (awww, a rofi v2 check, a wallust.sh compatibility step). The JaKooLit Hyprland-Dots scripts still call swww: 8 times in WallpaperSelect.sh, 2 times in Startup_Apps.conf.

findings.claim: How the JaKooLit installer is structured, and what it does well
findings.detail: install.sh: refuses to run as root; checks for PulseAudio, base-devel, whiptail (libnewt), an existing AUR helper, GDM/LightDM/LXDM and NVIDIA (lspci); shows a whiptail checklist; '--preset <file>' supplies the answers. It then calls one standalone script per component in install-scripts/: 00-base, pacman, yay/paru, 01-hypr-pkgs, pipewire, fonts, hyprland, sddm, sddm_theme, nvidia, nvidia_nouveau, gtk_themes, InputGroup, quickshell, xdph, bluetooth, thunar, zsh, zsh_pokemon, rog, dotfiles-main, 02-Final-Check. Each script can be re-run from the repo root. Global_functions.sh holds install_package, install_package_pacman and uninstall_package (each checks pacman -Q first, so re-runs are safe) and a spinner. Every step writes a timestamped log to Install-Logs/. There is an auto-install.sh (clone and run) and an uninstall.sh. The dotfiles come from the separate Hyprland-Dots repo via copy.sh, which has install, --upgrade and --express-upgrade modes and a version gate. It moves an existing ~/.config/<app> to '<app>-backup-back-up_MMDD_HHMM' (scripts/lib_backup.sh), restores UserConfigs/UserScripts so user overrides survive upgrades, and can trim old backups.

findings.claim: Mistakes in the JaKooLit installer that our installer should avoid
findings.detail: (1) pacman.sh runs 'sudo pacman -Sy' without -u, and this is still true in the LinuxBeginnings fork. A full upgrade only happens inside yay.sh/paru.sh, which runs only when no AUR helper is installed yet. So on machines that already have yay or paru, packages get installed after a bare -Sy, which is a partial upgrade (unsupported on Arch). (2) Only 'set -e' in the sourced Global_functions.sh: no -u and no pipefail. 'makepkg -si --noconfirm 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG" || exit 1' can never exit because tee's status hides makepkg's. (3) Each package is installed in its own background pacman transaction behind a spinner, and a failure only prints a message, so the script can finish with missing packages. (4) The preset file is loaded with 'source "$1"', which runs arbitrary bash. (5) auto-install.sh and dotfiles-main.sh run 'git stash && git pull', silently stashing local edits, and nothing pins a commit or verifies a signature. (6) pacman.conf is edited with sed without a backup, and packages such as dunst, mako, rofi and cachyos-hyprland-settings are removed with --noconfirm. (7) Package names are hard-coded and have gone stale: swww (JaKooLit repo), and nvidia-dkms (still in both the JaKooLit and LinuxBeginnings nvidia.sh). (8) No dry-run mode.

findings.claim: Primary sources for install-script safety practices
findings.detail: Arch: partial upgrades are unsupported (never 'pacman -Sy <pkg>'). --needed skips reinstalling up-to-date packages. makepkg refuses to run as root. BashFAQ/105: set -e is ignored inside if/&&/|| contexts and in functions called as conditions, and a pipeline only reports its last command unless pipefail is set, so add an ERR trap and explicit checks. gum 2.0.x is in [extra]; v2.0.0 moved to Bubble Tea v2 with 'no UX changes'. It provides confirm, choose (--limit/--no-limit), input (--password), filter, spin (--show-output), style and log (--structured --level). The Arch ISO (releng) does not include git, gum, whiptail/libnewt or jq. It does include archinstall, arch-install-scripts, btrfs-prs, reflector, grub, efibootmgr and iwd, and curl comes in as a pacman dependency.

rm -r /.snapshots

btrfs subvolume delete /.snapshots

recommendations: Install in two stages. Stage 1 runs from the Arch ISO: 'archinstall --config user_configuration.json --creds user_credentials.json --silent' (archinstall 4.4) sets up the disk, base system, bootloader, zram, PipeWire, NetworkManager, the Hyprland profile and SDDM. Stage 2 is your own script, run as your normal user after first boot, for AUR packages, snapshots and dotfiles. archinstall's custom_commands run as root in the chroot before genfstab, so they can't do the AUR or dotfile work.

Generate the disk part of the config for each machine: run 'archinstall --dry-run' on the target, or compute the root size as BYTES/1048576 - 1 - ESP_END_MiB. The parser rejects partitions that are misaligned or run past the end of the disk.

Disk layout: GPT, a FAT32 ESP of 4 GiB or more mounted at /boot (flags boot and esp), and btrfs with mount_options ["compress=zstd"]. Subvolumes: @, @home, @log, @pkg, plus your own @snapshots at /.snapshots. Leave btrfs_options.snapshot_config out and set up snapper in stage 2 using the wiki's flat-layout procedure.

Snapshots: if you pick Limine, use snapper, snap-pac, limine-mkinitcpio-hook and limine-snapper-sync. Add sd-btrfs-overlayfs to HOOKS, because archinstall uses a systemd initramfs. Then delete archinstall's EFI/arch-limine/limine.conf so it stops hiding $ESP/limine.conf. If you want zero manual steps instead, pick bootloader 'Grub' with snapshot_config Snapper: archinstall then sets up grub-btrfsd itself, but you get snapper's nested .snapshots. Test either path in a VM first.

AUR helper: default to yay, installed from yay-bin, which the upstream author packages. It is actively developed (v13, June 2026) and needs no compile on a fresh system. Let the script accept paru as an alternative, built from the 'paru' package. Never use paru-bin: it has no maintainer and is flagged out of date.

Keep the AUR list short and fixed, because the AUR had malware waves in 2026 and adoptions are currently disabled. The list is roughly: bibata-cursor-theme, maplemono-*, sddm-astronaut-theme, spicetify-cli, python-pywalfox, vesktop-bin, limine-snapper-sync, limine-mkinitcpio-hook, and optionally wallust or grimblast-git. Leave PKGBUILD review interactive. Take everything else from [extra]: hyprshot instead of grimblast, awww instead of swww, rofi 2.x, matugen instead of wallust, quickshell and dms-shell.

Make Chaotic-AUR an opt-in flag, off by default. It saves build time and covers most of the AUR list (not python-pywalfox, maplemono or plain wallust). But it builds automatically from AUR PKGBUILDs, so it adds a second party you have to trust.

Don't add the full CachyOS repos to vanilla Arch. The script replaces pacman, puts CachyOS repos above [core], and removal means reinstalling every native package. If you want a tuned kernel, use linux-zen from [extra] or linux-cachyos from Chaotic-AUR, or install CachyOS itself.

Dotfiles shared with NixOS: keep plain config files in a Stow layout, one package per app (home/<app>/.config/<app>). On Arch run 'stow --no-folding'. On NixOS use Home Manager xdg.configFile.<app>.source = config.lib.file.mkOutOfStoreSymlink with an absolute path string. Don't also use HM's Hyprland settings module, and avoid chezmoi templates, so there is one source of truth. For per-host differences, have the tracked config source an untracked local override file.

Build the stage-2 script like JaKooLit's modular per-component scripts, including logs, backups and the UserConfigs-style override layer, but fix its mistakes: use 'set -Eeuo pipefail' with an ERR trap; do one 'sudo pacman -Syu --needed' transaction and never 'pacman -Sy'; run 'pacman -Si' and an AUR RPC check before installing so renamed packages fail early; back up to a timestamped folder before replacing anything; support --dry-run and --yes; parse the preset file instead of sourcing it; pin the repo to a commit or tag instead of 'git stash && git pull'.

Use gum (in [extra]) for the menus, with a plain 'read' fallback when stdin is not a TTY or gum is missing. The Arch ISO has neither gum nor whiptail, and not git either, so the ISO-stage bootstrap should use only curl plus archinstall, or install git on the live ISO first.
If you encrypt the disk with LUKS and unlock with TPM2, re-enroll after the mkinitcpio 42 update (Arch news 2026-09-22).
deprecations_pitfalls: archinstall 4.4 still reads some old config keys (top-level audio_config, bootloader + uki, disk_encryption, parallel_downloads, !users, !root-password, additional-repositories). Generate new configs with the current keys: app_config.audio_config, bootloader_config, disk_config.disk_encryption, pacman_config and --creds users.

archinstall's docs example (docs/installing/guided.rst) is out of date: it uses partition 'length' and the old Size fields, but the 4.4 parser reads 'size' {value, unit, sector_size}. Use examples/config-sample.json or '--dry-run' output instead.

gfx_driver 'Nvidia (proprietary)' now fails with an error. nvidia and nvidia-dkms were replaced by nvidia-open(-dkms) in December 2025. GTX 10xx and older need nvidia-580xx-dkms from the AUR. JaKooLit's nvidia.sh, including the LinuxBeginnings fork, still installs nvidia-dkms.
swww is gone: awww provides and replaces it in pacman, but ships only 'awww' and 'awww-daemon'. Scripts that call 'swww img', such as the archived JaKooLit Hyprland-Dots, fail at runtime.
rofi-wayland no longer exists; use rofi 2.0.0. hyprland-qtutils is replaced by hyprland-guiutils. ttf-maple doesn't exist; Maple Mono is maplemono-* in the AUR.
Hyprland-specific tools with no official package: grimblast (AUR only as grimblast-git, last modified January 2024) and wlogout (AUR, last modified 2024-04-22).

'pacman -Sy <pkg>' and a bare 'pacman -Sy' before installing are partial upgrades, which Arch does not support. JaKooLit's pacman.sh does this, and no full upgrade follows when an AUR helper is already installed.
Without pipefail, 'makepkg ... | tee log || exit 1' never exits on a failed build. BashFAQ/105 also lists the cases where set -e doesn't fire (if, &&, ||, functions used as conditions).

If you enable archinstall's snapshot_config and also define @snapshots at /.snapshots, create-config is likely to fail. And archinstall's own snapper setup gives you nested .snapshots rather than the wiki's flat layout.

archinstall's Limine install writes EFI/arch-limine/limine.conf. Limine reads '<EFI app path>/limine.conf' first, so that file hides the $ESP/limine.conf that limine-entry-tool and limine-snapper-sync maintain.
grub-btrfs-overlayfs works only with a busybox initramfs, and archinstall uses systemd hooks by default. For Limine, use sd-btrfs-overlayfs; btrfs-overlayfs is incompatible with systemd hooks.

limine-snapper-sync needs the kernels on the same ESP as limine.conf (boot():), /usr/lib/modules inside the root subvolume, and an ESP of about 4 GiB or more (archinstall's default is 1 GiB). Snapshots taken before it was installed can't be booted.
paru-bin is orphaned and flagged out of date since 2025-12-13, so don't bootstrap from it. paru hasn't had a release since July 2025, while yay released v13 in June 2026.

AUR security in 2026: malicious adoptions and updates (Arch news 2026-06-12), and package adoption disabled as of about 2026-07-31. Chaotic-AUR builds automatically from AUR sources, so compromised updates probably reach it too.

The CachyOS repo script installs CachyOS's own pacman build, puts its repos above [core] (overriding many Arch packages), and warns that Intel 12th gen and newer can be wrongly detected as x86-64-v4. Removing it needs 'pacman -Suuy' plus reinstalling every native package.

JaKooLit/Arch-Hyprland and Hyprland-Dots moved to LinuxBeginnings in March 2026, and JaKooLit's last commit is 2026-02-22. Don't copy package lists or script patterns from the archived repos without checking them.
JaKooLit's '--preset' loads the preset with 'source', which runs it as bash. auto-install.sh runs 'git stash && git pull', which silently stashes your local changes.
custom_commands in archinstall run as root before genfstab, so there is no fstab yet and makepkg won't run.
Home Manager's mkOutOfStoreSymlink with a relative ./path under flakes points into the Nix store, so changes aren't live. Pass an absolute string such as "${config.home.homeDirectory}/dotfiles/...".

'stow --adopt' moves your existing files into the repo, overwriting what's there. Check first with -n (simulate), and use --no-folding so apps don't write into the repo through a folded directory symlink.
archinstall's Hyprland profile installs dunst and wofi. Running dunst alongside swaync or a Quickshell notification service means two notification daemons, so remove or mask the one you don't use.
The Arch ISO has no git, gum, whiptail or jq. Plan the ISO-stage bootstrap around curl plus archinstall.
mkinitcpio 42 changes PCR measurements, so TPM2 LUKS unlocking needs re-enrolling (Arch news 2026-09-22).

findings.claim: NyArch is an Arch-based distro built with archiso and EzArcher. GNOME is the main edition, a KDE edition shipped in 26.04, and the Hyprland spin is still only an idea.
findings.detail: The main README calls it 'a Linux distribution made for weebs, based on ArchLinux and EzArcher' and says to 'use another enstablished distribution as a daily drive'. Latest release: 26.04 'Gyro', 2026-04-29. It added a KDE edition with Qt rewrites of the Nyarch apps, a new GRUB theme, new Plymouth themes, a new Fish config and NekoPlay. Bazaar replaced GNOME Software. Nyarch apps now come as pacman packages from [nyarch-repo] instead of Flatpaks. The wiki's Future Projects table lists the 'Hyprland Spin' with status 'Idea' / 'In begining phase'. The wiki link to TotallyDIO/NyarchHyprland returns 404.

findings.claim: NyarchLinux/Nyarch-Hyprland is an unmodified-looking fork of linkfrg/dotfiles, built on the Ignis widget framework. Its last commit was 2025-03-17.
findings.detail: The README is still titled "linkfrg's Hyprland(and Ignis!) dotfiles". It generates Material colors from the wallpaper and has a control center and a settings app. The repo contains .config/hypr (default/ and custom/ split), ignis/ and a 'Material' GTK theme. dependencies.txt lists hyprland, ignis-git, dart-sass, python-materialyoucolor, hyprlock, grimblast-git, kitty, thunar, papirus-icon-theme, ttf-jetbrains-mono-nerd, among others. License is GPL-3.0. The config uses pre-Lua hyprlang syntax.

findings.claim: The Ignis MaterialService in Nyarch-Hyprland is a compact Material You pipeline you can reuse.
findings.detail: How it works: shrink the wallpaper, run QuantizeCelebi(128), take Score.score()[0], then SchemeTonalSpot(hct, dark_mode, 0.0) and dump every MaterialDynamicColors role to hex. It renders Jinja templates (colors-hyprland.conf, colors-kitty.conf, colors.scss, gtk.css, swaylock) into ~/.cache/ignis/material/. It then runs 'pkill -SIGUSR1 kitty' and toggles gsettings gtk-theme Adwaita→Material and color-scheme to force a GTK reload. Hyprland reads the output with source=~/.cache/ignis/material/dark_colors-hyprland.conf and col.active_border = $primary.

findings.claim: GNOME version tracks Arch. The exact version on the 26.04 ISO was not verified.
findings.detail: Arch extra has gnome-shell 50.5 and gdm 50.3 today. Nyarcher, the installer that applies the customizations on other distros, refuses GNOME below 47. The bundled material-you-colors extension declares shell-version 45–49. Nyarch's dconf sets disable-extension-version-validation=true so the extensions still load on newer shells. The dconf also contains a stale welcome-dialog-last-shown-version='43.2'.

- fail: '>-<'
A UwU face image also exists.

The password prompt reads 'Pawsword? :3c', with 'Paw' in #b4e6ff. Password bullets are paw prints cycling through pink, hotpink, lightblue and darkblue. Assets come in 720p, 1080p, 1440p and 4k and are picked by screen height. There is a manual resolution override for multi-monitor setups.

The script header says it is based on arch-logo-new.script, (C) 2009 Canonical, GPL-2.0-or-later. Credits name Cloveian for the adaptation. plymouthd.conf sets Theme=nyarch-logo and ShowDelay=0. GRUB passes 'quiet splash'.

findings.claim: The GRUB theme is NyarchLinux/Nyarch-Grub-Theme (MIT). Calamares installs it as a package.
findings.detail:
The theme has theme.txt, background.png and images/. Its README says it contains art from the ventoy-themes GRUB theme, the FlatSense GRUB theme and a background by raviolimavioli (pixiv artwork 89596288). The LICENSE is MIT, Copyright (c) 2023 Diego Duarte.

The Calamares 'grubtheme' module detects the resolution with xrandr and runs pacman -U on /opt/ezrepo/grub-theme-Nyarch*.pkg.tar.zst; the ISO ships grub-theme-Nyarch-1.2-1-any. /etc/default/grub sets GRUB_DISTRIBUTOR="Nyarch". There is also /etc/grub.d/39_power_menu. Legacy BIOS boot uses syslinux splash.png, an edited version of RavioliMavioli's Arch Linux art.

findings.claim: The login screen is plain GDM with a Nyarch logo. GDM Material You theming is optional and not the default.
findings.detail: The gdm dconf db sets [org/gnome/login-screen] logo='/usr/share/nyarch/nyarch_logo.png'. gdm/custom.conf enables AutomaticLogin=live, which only applies to the live ISO user. The material-you-colors README describes optional GDM theming via gdm-tools (set-gdm-theme), but Nyarch does not apply it by default.

findings.claim: No custom sound theme or cute notification sounds were found.
findings.detail: There is no usr/share/sounds in the repo, no sounds directory in skel and no org/gnome/desktop/sound key in the dconf dumps. The search was not exhaustive (I did not grep every binary), but a sound theme would normally live in one of those places.

findings.claim: Fetch art uses fastfetch with a kitty-protocol PNG logo and truecolor ASCII fallbacks. nyaofetch picks the variant by terminal width.
findings.detail:
config.jsonc (header 'by Bina') uses logo.source ~/.config/fastfetch/logo.png, type 'kitty', height 14. Keys are '~ ' in color 34, with a '~~~~' separator. config_extended.jsonc uses ' ➜  ' as the separator.

The ASCII files ascii50/60/70/90 are ANSI 24-bit colored renders of the cat logo. /usr/local/bin/nyaofetch shows the PNG when $KITTY_WINDOW_ID or $KONSOLE_VERSION is set, otherwise the ASCII sized to `tput cols`. nekofetch runs nyaofetch then 'exec bash'. The fish greeting runs fastfetch. Nyarch Tour's 'I use Nyarch, btw' page runs 'kitty nekofetch'.

findings.claim: Small weeb touches: nyay, nyaura and pacnyan wrappers, pacman ILoveCandy, nyancat, and newbie-joke aliases.
findings.detail: /usr/local/bin/nyay runs `yay "$@"`, nyaura runs aura and pacnyan runs pacman. pacman.conf enables Color and ILoveCandy. nyancat is in packages.x86_64. The fish config aliases please='sudo', apt='man pacman' and apt-get='man pacman'. None of these are notifications; no cute notification strings were found.

findings.claim: Terminal setup: kitty with transparency and cursor trail, a transparent GNOME Terminal, and pywal sequences in bash.
findings.detail:
kitty.conf sets background_opacity 0.82, cursor_trail 1, wayland_titlebar_color system and linux_display_server x11. The dconf gives the gnome-terminal-transparency profile background-transparency-percent=7. gnome-console is also installed. .bashrc cats ~/.cache/wal/sequences, and skel pre-seeds ~/.cache/wal for kitty, rofi, waybar, sway and other templates.

fish config exists in skel, but fish is not in packages.x86_64 at HEAD; NyarchScript offers 'Install fish'. The 26.04 notes mention a 'New Fish shell configuration'.

findings.claim: The default wallpaper set is 'Arch-chan' (light and dark files). It is not in git: the ISO build downloads it at build time as NyarchCopy.tar.gz.
findings.detail:
customize_airootfs.sh runs `wget https://nyarchlinux.moe/NyarchCopy.tar.gz`. Despite the .gz name, that file is an uncompressed tar. It contains default.jpg, default-l.jpg, default-d.jpg, acchan.jpg/png and Arch-chan.xml. The XML is a gnome-wp-list entry named 'Arch-chan' pointing at default-l.jpg and default-d.jpg. The dark file has the same byte size as acchan.jpg. dconf points picture-uri at /usr/share/backgrounds/default.jpg.

The skel backgrounds folder adds Nyarch_Wallpaper.png, Nyarch_Wallpaper_Name.png, archlinux.png, nyaight-neko.png and a wallpaperflare 'anime-girls-picture-in-picture…cat-girl-blonde' jpg.

findings.claim: Nyarch Assistant is a GPL-3.0 fork of Newelle that adds a Live2D, LivePNG or VRM waifu avatar with a tsundere Arch-chan persona.
findings.detail:
Features: expressions and motions, 'Harem Support', TTS/STT, MCP tools, a mini window ('nyarchassistant --mini'), and running terminal commands.

The default Live2D model is 'Arch/arch chan model0.model3.json', downloaded from http://mirror.nyarchlinux.moe/Arch.tar.xz and rendered with NyarchLinux/live2d-lipsync-viewer. VRM goes through NyarchLinux/VRM-Web-Viewer. The personality prompt begins "Hey there, it's Arch-Chan! But, um, you can call me Acchan…".

The wiki says the default Demo API allows 10 requests per day and uses gemini-flash-2.0. It recommends Ollama for privacy and VoiceVox (in Docker) for Japanese TTS. Upstream Newelle is in nixpkgs as `newelle` 1.5.0 (gpl3Plus).

findings.claim: DesktopPuppet puts Arch-chan (Acchan) on the desktop as a Live2D pet. Its best-supported compositor is Hyprland.
findings.detail: The README says 'only Hyprland is fully supported for now'. It uses Gtk4LayerShell with a transparent WebKit 6.0 webview, on the OVERLAY or BACKGROUND layer. Its Hyprland interface calls `hyprctl cursorpos` and `hyprctl monitors -j` to follow the mouse. It is installed from Nyarch Assistant's avatar settings. The README suggests hyprlang binds using cli.sh set-overlay background/overlay and sendshortcut to title:nyarchassistant. On GNOME it needs NyarchPetGnomeExtension. License GPL-3.0.

findings.claim: Nyarch Tour, Wizard, Customize, Updater and Scripts are small GTK4/libadwaita apps (GPL-3.0) tied to GNOME and to Nyarch itself.
findings.detail:
- Tour: carousel pages including 'Welcome to Nyarch', 'Material You', 'Nyarch Customize', 'Catgirl Downloader', 'Read manga with Komikku', 'Listen to your favourite weeb radio with Shortwave', Fragments, Lollypop, Webapp Manager, Bazaar, 'I use Nyarch, btw', 'Your dream waifu at your command' and NekoPlay. It autostarts once on first login via /usr/share/ezarcher/Scripts/autostart.sh.
- Wizard: suggests apps by category (Office, Gaming, Communication, Audio, Image, Video, Dev, Notes).
- Customize: switches layouts by enabling or disabling dash-to-panel, arcmenu and dash-to-dock. It has toggles for Material You, accent colors, blur, wobbly, magic lamp, cube, tray, desktop icons and logo, all through gsettings and gnome-extensions.
- Updater: handles release, pacman, Flatpak and AUR updates; its README says it only works on Nyarch.
- Scripts: GUI for pacman and reflector tasks, kernels, and Chaotic or Nyarch repo setup.

findings.claim: Catgirl Downloader and Waifu Downloader are GPL-3.0 GTK4 image fetchers. NekoPlay is an anime-focused video player.
findings.detail: CatgirlDownloader pulls from nekos.moe (/api/v1/random/image, blocking NSFW by default), api.waifu.im and danbooru. WaifuDownloader uses waifu.im. NekoPlay is a fork of Cine (MPV-based) with '4K Anime upscaling' and a 90-second opening-skip button.

findings.claim: The Nyarch pacman repo is a normal Arch repo with its own mirrors and keyring.
findings.detail: pacman.conf has [nyarch-repo] Include=/etc/pacman.d/nyarch-mirrorlist. The mirrors are de-pkgmirror.nyarchlinux.moe, nymirror.nyarchlinux.moe and mousecorp.xyz. Packages include nyarchassistant 1.5.0, catgirldownloader, nekoplay, nyarchtour/wizard/customize/updater/script plus Qt variants, adwaita-material-you, python-materialyoucolor 3.0.2, python-pywal16 and kde-material-you-colors. The keyring is the nyarch-keyring package.

findings.claim: The current Hyprland wiki uses Lua config: 'Since Hyprland 0.55, hyprlang is deprecated in favor of lua'. Arch extra ships Hyprland 0.56.2.
findings.detail:
The config lives at ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua. Examples from the wiki:
- hl.window_rule({ match = { class = "kitty" }, opacity = "0.8 0.8" })
- hl.layer_rule({ match = { namespace = "waybar" }, blur = true })
- hl.bind(...)
- hl.env(...)
- hl.on("hyprland.start", function () hl.exec_cmd(...) end)

The window-rule effects list includes no_wobble, which suggests native wobble exists on latest git; I did not check whether it is in the 0.56 tag. Nyarch-Hyprland and the DesktopPuppet README both use the older hyprlang syntax. Nyarch-Hyprland's windowrule lines are the legacy v1 form.

findings.claim: Availability of replacement tools, checked on 2026-09-25.
findings.detail:
Arch extra: matugen 4.2.0, adw-gtk-theme 6.5 (the old adw-gtk3 name returns nothing), plymouth, fastfetch 2.68.1, kitty 0.48.2, komikku, quickshell 0.3.1, hyprlock 0.9.6, hypridle, swaync, awww 0.12.1, nyancat, bazaar.

AUR: python-materialyoucolor 3.0.2, python-pywal16, tela-circle-icon-theme-git, newelle 1.5.0, wayle 0.7.0, nyarchassistant 1.2.5 (stale compared with 1.5.0 in nyarch-repo), catgirldownloader 0.5, gnome-terminal-transparency, bibata-cursor-theme, sddm-astronaut-theme. ignis-git (listed by Nyarch-Hyprland) was not returned by the AUR RPC.

nixpkgs HEAD: matugen 4.2.0, newelle, komikku, shortwave, fragments, lollypop, tela-circle-icon-theme (colorVariants is an enum, so no arbitrary hex), adw-gtk3, pywal16, hyprlock, hypridle, quickshell, fastfetch, nyancat, gearlever, bazaar, swaynotificationcenter, awww, hyprpaper, mpvpaper, waypaper, bibata-cursors, sddm-astronaut, catppuccin-sddm, fuzzel, walker, rofi, cliphist, cava, kdotool, gtk4-layer-shell, wayle, and python3Packages.materialyoucolor. No ignis or Nyarch app packages. aliases.nix: `hyprpanel` throws ('archived, consider using wayle', 2026-07-21); `swww` is renamed to `awww` (2026-03-22).

findings.claim: Licenses split cleanly between code (reusable) and art (mostly unclear or third-party).
findings.detail:
Code:
- NyarchLinux repo, apps, Nyarcher, Nyarch-Hyprland and the material-you-colors extension: GPL-3.0.
- GRUB theme: MIT.
- Plymouth script: GPL-2.0-or-later.

Art (from the credits files):
- Logo and name come from a Reddit post ('someone posted uwuntu so i made nyarch'), with no license stated.
- An earlier default wallpaper was an upscaled wallhaven mpg7qk by RakhaKun.
- Nyarch logo wallpapers come from r/LinuxFurries.
- The other catgirl wallpaper is from wallpaperflare.
- The 24.04 wallpaper is from pixiv user 14801956.
- The Calamares background is a modified r/fatestaynight image.
- The GRUB mascot and the BIOS splash are by RavioliMavioli.

A secondary source (Ivon's blog, citing the artist's Pixiv profile) says RavioliMavioli's works are CC-BY 4.0. The Speykious/arch-chan archive says its Arch-chan Live2D/Inochi2D model is CC0 1.0. Credits do not name an artist for nyaight-neko.png or the current 'Arch-chan' default wallpaper; I did not determine them.

recommendations: Material You ('Material UwU') pipeline: replace the GNOME extension with matugen (Arch extra `matugen` 4.2.0; nixpkgs `matugen` 4.2.0). One `matugen image <wall>` run should render templates for ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css and gtk-3.0/gtk.css (with adw-gtk3), Hyprland border colors, kitty, the bar/notification CSS and the lockscreen. If you want Nyarch's exact libadwaita color mapping, use `adwmu dark -w <wall> -a` from adwaita-material-you instead. Keep the Flatpak global override `filesystems=xdg-config/gtk-4.0;xdg-config/gtk-3.0` so Flatpaks follow the theme.

Port after_wp_change.sh as a matugen post_hook. Pass {{colors.primary.default.hex}} without the '#' to the Nyarch Tela-circle fork's install.sh: `install.sh -n Tela-circle-MaterialYou <hex>`. Then run `gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface icon-theme Tela-circle-MaterialYou-<hex>` and prune old variants, as Nyarch does. On NixOS, run this at user level into ~/.local/share/icons, because the nixpkgs tela-circle-icon-theme only accepts named colorVariants.

Replace each GNOME extension with a Hyprland piece:
- blur-my-shell → decoration.blur plus a layer_rule with blur=true on your bar and launcher namespaces.
- dash-to-dock / dash-to-panel / arcmenu → a Quickshell (Arch extra `quickshell` 0.3.1; nixpkgs `quickshell`) or wayle (AUR `wayle`; nixpkgs `wayle`) bar and dock, plus a launcher such as fuzzel, walker or rofi (all in nixpkgs).
- appindicator / trayIconsReloaded → the bar's SNI tray.
- arch-update → a bar module around `checkupdates` on Arch; skip it on NixOS.
- compiz wobbly / magic lamp → Hyprland animations (bezier 'quart' slide like Nyarch-Hyprland). Latest-git Hyprland also has a wobble option; check your tagged version.
- gsconnect → KDE Connect.
- user-theme MaterialYou shell → the matugen-rendered bar CSS.

Write the Hyprland config in Lua (~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua) for 0.55+ (Arch has 0.56.2). Translate Nyarch-Hyprland's hyprlang look: gaps 5/20, border 2, rounding 15, blur size 12 passes 4, shadow range 30, 'quart' bezier 0.25,1,0.5,1. Use hl.window_rule, hl.layer_rule, hl.bind with hl.dsp.exec_cmd, and hl.on('hyprland.start'). If you use home-manager's hyprland module on NixOS, check whether it emits Lua or hyprlang for your Hyprland version; I did not verify this.

Plymouth: reuse the nyarch-logo theme for the OwO/paw LUKS prompt.
- Arch: copy the folder to /usr/share/plymouth/themes, set Theme=nyarch-logo in plymouthd.conf, add the plymouth hook and 'quiet splash', and rebuild the initramfs.
- NixOS: package the folder with stdenvNoCC.mkDerivation into $out/share/plymouth/themes/nyarch-logo. Rewrite the hard-coded /usr/share paths in nyarch-logo.plymouth (ImageDir/ScriptFile) to $out, then set boot.plymouth.enable, boot.plymouth.theme = "nyarch-logo" and boot.plymouth.themePackages. Use boot.initrd.systemd for a graphical LUKS prompt. This is an untested sketch.

GRUB: use Nyarch-Grub-Theme (MIT). On Arch set GRUB_THEME="/boot/grub/themes/Nyarch-theme/theme.txt" and run grub-mkconfig. On NixOS set boot.loader.grub.theme to the Nyarch-theme directory of a fetchFromGitHub source (untested sketch). Keep the MIT notice and credit RavioliMavioli for the background.

Login screen: Nyarch only puts a logo on GDM. On Hyprland, use SDDM with sddm-astronaut-theme (AUR; nixpkgs `sddm-astronaut`) or greetd with a GTK greeter. Pick Arch-chan art rather than the Nyarch logo, since the logo's license is unclear, and theme it from matugen colors. hyprlock (Arch extra 0.9.6; nixpkgs `hyprlock`) replaces the GNOME lock screen; Nyarch-Hyprland used it.

Fetch and terminal: reuse fastfetch config.jsonc, config_extended.jsonc, logo.png and the ascii50–90 files, plus the nyaofetch/nekofetch scripts, which work unchanged in kitty on Hyprland. Reuse the kitty settings (background_opacity 0.82, cursor_trail 1) but drop `linux_display_server x11` so kitty runs native Wayland. Feed kitty colors from matugen and reload with `pkill -SIGUSR1 kitty`, as the Ignis service does. Add a fish_greeting that runs fastfetch.

Cute aliases: on Arch add nyay→yay, pacnyan→pacman, please→sudo, and enable Color and ILoveCandy in pacman.conf. On NixOS put equivalents in environment.shellAliases or home.shellAliases, for example a 'nyaa-rebuild' alias for nixos-rebuild. Install nyancat (Arch extra; nixpkgs `nyancat`). Nyarch has no sound theme, so pick your own freely.

Waifu layer: install Nyarch Assistant as the Flatpak bundle (works on any distro; on NixOS enable services.flatpak) or from nyarch-repo on Arch. On NixOS, use nixpkgs `newelle` if you don't need the avatar. Run DesktopPuppet as the Hyprland desktop pet (it needs gtk4-layer-shell and webkitgtk-6.0). Convert its README binds to Lua hl.bind calls: SUPER+F7/F8 set-overlay, SUPER+F9/F10 send shortcuts to title:nyarchassistant. Use Ollama instead of the 10-requests/day demo API.

Wallpaper flow: use Catgirl Downloader or Waifu Downloader (Flatpak bundles; AUR catgirldownloader) to fetch images. Set them with awww (Arch extra and nixpkgs `awww`; `swww` is renamed) or hyprpaper, then run matugen. matugen's [config.wallpaper] command can call `awww img` directly.

Don't port Nyarch Tour, Wizard, Customize or Updater. They assume GNOME and Nyarch. Their jobs are better done by a first-login script (Arch) or by declarative modules (NixOS). Use Tour's page list (Komikku, Shortwave, Fragments, Lollypop, Bazaar, NekoPlay, Assistant) as the app checklist; Komikku, Shortwave, Fragments, Lollypop and Bazaar are in nixpkgs and Arch.

Fonts: match Nyarch with ttf-jetbrains-mono-nerd and noto-fonts-cjk so Japanese anime and manga titles render, plus noto-fonts. Pick a kitty font you actually install; Nyarch's 'SF Mono Ligaturized' isn't shipped. Choose a cursor yourself (Nyarch uses the default Adwaita); bibata-cursor-theme (AUR) and nixpkgs `bibata-cursors` are available.

Licensing:
- Freely reusable with notices: all Nyarch code and configs (GPL-3.0: apps, dotfiles, scripts, Nyarch-Hyprland, the material-you extension), the Plymouth script (GPL-2.0+) and the GRUB theme (MIT).
- Reuse with attribution: RavioliMavioli art (Arch-chan/Acchan, GRUB background), reported CC-BY 4.0. Confirm on the artist's page.
- Don't redistribute publicly: the Nyarch logo (Reddit origin), the r/LinuxFurries, wallpaperflare and wallhaven wallpapers, and nyaight-neko.png. Keep them local.
deprecations_pitfalls: Hyprland 0.55+ deprecates hyprlang in favor of Lua (~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua), and Arch ships 0.56.2. Nyarch-Hyprland (last commit 2025-03-17) and the DesktopPuppet README binds use hyprlang, and Nyarch-Hyprland's `windowrule = float,^(kitty)$` lines are the legacy v1 form. Rewrite them; don't copy them.
The Hyprland wiki you land on by default documents latest git. Use the version selector to read the docs for your tagged release (check with `hyprctl version`).
nixpkgs aliases: `hyprpanel` now throws ('archived, consider using wayle', added 2026-07-21), and `swww` is renamed to `awww` (2026-03-22). Older rice guides using either will break on NixOS.
Ignis, the shell behind Nyarch-Hyprland, has no nixpkgs package, and the AUR RPC did not return the `ignis-git` its dependencies.txt names. Building on Ignis means a flake or manual install.
nyarch-logo.plymouth hard-codes ImageDir and ScriptFile to /usr/share/plymouth/themes/nyarch-logo. NixOS needs a path substitution or the theme won't load.
The nixpkgs `tela-circle-icon-theme` colorVariants is a fixed enum (standard, blue, pink…). Nyarch's per-wallpaper hex icons need the NyarchLinux fork's install.sh run at user level.

after_wp_change.sh depends on gsettings and on the GNOME extension writing ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css. On Hyprland, trigger it from matugen or adwmu instead. Also make sure gsettings/dconf and xdg-desktop-portal-gtk are available so GTK apps read color-scheme.

Nyarch Customize and Updater assume GNOME extensions or a Nyarch install; the Updater README says it only works on Nyarch. The AUR `nyarchassistant` is 1.2.5, stale compared with 1.5.0 in nyarch-repo. Prefer the Flatpak bundle or nyarch-repo.
Adding [nyarch-repo] to a plain Arch install needs the nyarch-keyring and nyarch-mirrorlist packages first. The README calls Nyarch itself not suitable as a daily driver.
The default wallpaper is not in git. It comes from https://nyarchlinux.moe/NyarchCopy.tar.gz, which is an uncompressed tar despite the .gz name; `tar -xzf` fails, so use `tar -xf`.
kitty.conf in NyArch sets `linux_display_server x11` and a font that isn't shipped ('SF Mono Ligaturized'). Remove or replace both on Hyprland.
The fish config ships in skel, but fish is not in packages.x86_64 at HEAD. Don't assume Nyarch's default shell is fish.

The bundled material-you-colors metadata only lists GNOME Shell 45–49; Nyarch forces loading on newer shells with disable-extension-version-validation=true. This only matters if you keep a GNOME fallback session.
The wiki link to TotallyDIO/NyarchHyprland returns 404, so there is no maintained official Hyprland spin to copy.

Nyarch Assistant's default Demo API (gemini-flash-2.0, 10 requests/day per the wiki) is a showcase only. Configure Ollama or your own provider. Enabling terminal command execution and home filesystem access in the Flatpak reduces sandboxing.

Art licensing is mostly undocumented. Only RavioliMavioli's CC-BY 4.0 (reported by a secondary source) and the CC0 arch-chan model archive give clear reuse terms. Treat the other wallpapers and the logo as all-rights-reserved.
NyarchLinux/AgeVerification is satire, not a real component. Leave it out of any rice.

findings.claim: Google Sans Flex is open source (OFL-1.1) and has a roundness axis, but it is barely packaged
findings.detail: Released Nov 18, 2025 under OFL. google/fonts ofl/googlesansflex/METADATA.pb shows license OFL and the file GoogleSansFlex[GRAD,ROND,opsz,slnt,wdth,wght].ttf. ROND controls rounded terminals, which suits a cute UI. The upstream repo googlefonts/googlesans-flex is active (releases v4.007). AUR ttf-google-sans-flex-variable 1.0.0 was created 2026-09-25, has 0 votes, and downloads the unpinned main-branch TTF. nixpkgs has no dedicated attr (by-name google-sans-flex returns 404). The google/fonts revision pinned by nixpkgs `google-fonts` (5174b333…, 2026-03-13) does not contain ofl/googlesansflex (404), so `google-fonts.override { fonts = ["GoogleSansFlex"]; }` will not work yet. Anime: 13atm01/GRUB-Theme (GPL-3.0 file, active 2026-09-15) and xandemon/anime-grub-theme (GPL-3.0, last commit 2026-01-29). Their character art belongs to the anime and VTuber rights holders, so the GPL does not clear it.

findings.claim: fastfetch image logos: which type works in which terminal
findings.detail: Logo types in the schema: auto, builtin, small, file, file-raw, data, data-raw, command-raw, sixel, kitty, kitty-direct, kitty-icat, iterm, chafa, raw, none. From the wiki: kitty-direct works in WezTerm, Warp, Kitty and Ghostty. It is the fastest, accepts PNG only on Kitty and Ghostty, needs --logo-width and --logo-height, and does not work in Konsole. kitty and sixel require fastfetch built with imagemagick. kitty-icat needs `kitten` and has tmux issues. command-raw was added in 2.45.0 and runs a command such as pokemon-colorscripts. Arch extra/fastfetch is 2.68.1. presets/ contains all, archey, ci, neofetch, paleofetch and screenfetch .jsonc files plus an examples/ directory with 37 .jsonc presets.

findings.claim: Firefox theme status
findings.detail: textfox: MPL-2.0, active 2026-09-10. It recommends coloring via the Firefox Color extension and ships a flake with homeManagerModules.default (textfox.enable, profiles, config). It is not in nixpkgs or AUR. catppuccin/firefox: MIT, just Firefox Color links, last commit 2023-07-18. catppuccin/nix has a home-manager firefox.nix module. ShyFox: MPL-2.0; its README says "This theme is not maintained right now and can be broken" (last commit 2025-01-21). Cascade: MIT; the original author announced he stepped back and moved it to the cascadefox org, which last committed on 2026-05-23.

findings.claim: Spicetify and Discord theming
findings.detail: spicetify-cli (LGPL-2.1) is AUR spicetify-cli 2.45.1 and nixpkgs spicetify-cli. Gerg-L/spicetify-nix (GPL-3.0, active 2026-09-21) has themes.catppuccin (colorScheme mocha|frappe|latte|macchiato), themes.comfy and themes.text. Comfy-Themes/Spicetify is WTFPL (last commit 2025-12-25). catppuccin/spicetify is MIT. spicetify-themes (includes 'text') is MIT and active. Discord: Vesktop (GPL-3.0) is AUR vesktop-bin 1.6.7 (maintained by Vendicated) or vesktop, and nixpkgs vesktop. catppuccin/discord (MIT) is applied with an @import URL and supports accent suffixes. refact0r/midnight-discord and refact0r/system24 (MIT, both active) have catppuccin-mocha, catppuccin-macchiato, rose-pine and rose-pine-moon flavors. catppuccin/nix has a vesktop.nix module.

findings.claim: No well-maintained 'kawaii' freedesktop sound theme exists; public-domain or official packages are the safe choices
findings.detail: elementary/sound-theme is released into the public domain (Unlicense text) and active 2026-04-19. It is Arch extra/sound-theme-elementary 1.1.0 and nixpkgs pantheon.elementary-sound-theme. Other packaged themes: Arch extra ocean-sound-theme 6.7.5 (nixpkgs kdePackages.ocean-sound-theme), deepin-sound-theme and sound-theme-freedesktop. AUR has yaru-sound-theme and sound-theme-smooth (license custom:combined). materia-sound-theme is GPL-3.0 but dormant since 2020. The only 'cute' one found, coffeeking/chihuahua-sound-theme, has no license and was last touched in 2018, so do not redistribute it.

findings.claim: None of the requested wallpaper repos give a clean license for their images
findings.detail: orangci/walls-catppuccin-mocha: no LICENSE; the disclaimer says the images are "sourced from many, many, many sources… I did not make any of these". D3Ext/aesthetic-wallpapers: MIT LICENSE file, but images come from "Unixporn, Wallhaven, Reddit and Github". dharmx/walls: no LICENSE; includes anime, boccha and evangelion folders. FrenzyExists/wallpapers: MIT-style LICENSE, but it contains Anime and Pixelart collections of third-party art; last commit 2022. rose-pine/wallpapers: LICENSE file is CC0-1.0, yet the README says "All photographs below are licensed as CC BY-SA 4.0", and it has Anime and Manga sections. AngelJumbo/gruvbox-wallpapers: no LICENSE; the README says original sources are "often unknown" and recommends a reverse image search for any use beyond personal. zhichaoh/catppuccin-wallpapers: MIT file copied from Catppuccin; last commit 2022-08-23.

findings.claim: catppuccin/nix covers most of the rice
findings.detail: catppuccin/nix (MIT, v26.05, active 2026-09-16). Home-manager modules include cursors, gtk (icon only), hyprland, hyprlock, kitty, ghostty, foot, waybar, mako, swaync, dunst, fuzzel, rofi, tofi, wlogout, wleave, firefox, vesktop, vscode, neovim, spotify-player, cava, btop, starship, fish, zsh-syntax-highlighting, kvantum, qt5ct and yazi. NixOS modules include cursors, fcitx5, grub, gtk, limine, plymouth, sddm and tty.

findings.claim: Pokemon terminal art: the code is open source, the sprites are not
findings.detail: pokemon-colorscripts: GitLab project license is MIT, last activity 2026-06-02. AUR pokemon-colorscripts-git; nixpkgs pokemon-colorscripts (0-unstable-2024-10-19). krabby: GPL-3.0; AUR krabby-bin 0.3.0; nixpkgs krabby 0.3.0. Both render Pokémon sprites, which are Nintendo/Game Freak IP. Installing them from the distro is fine; bundling the sprites in your own repo is not. I did not check the upstream projects' own statements about sprite licensing.

recommendations: Default palette: Catppuccin Mocha (dark) and Latte (light) with a pink or mauve accent. It has the widest maintained coverage (SDDM, GRUB, Limine, Plymouth, cursors, Papirus folders, Discord, Spicetify, Firefox Color, nvim/VS Code), and catppuccin/nix v26.05 has NixOS and home-manager modules for most of these. Offer matugen + adw-gtk3 as an optional 'dynamic from wallpaper' mode.

GTK: use Magnetic Catppuccin (nixpkgs magnetic-catppuccin-gtk, accent pink, shade dark, with --libadwaita for GTK4) or Colloid with tweaks=[catppuccin] and themeVariants=[pink]. Do not use catppuccin/gtk (archived), and on NixOS avoid murrine-based themes (Graphite, Vimix, Lavanda, Layan, Rose-Pine-GTK, Sweet, etc. were removed 2026-07-22).
Icons: Papirus-Dark with catppuccin-papirus-folders (cat-mocha-pink) as the default. Tela-circle pink or Colloid (scheme catppuccin, color pink) as alternates.

Cursor: catppuccin-cursors.mochaPink as the Catppuccin match, or Bibata Modern (GPL-3.0, hyprcursor fork available) as the neutral default. Enable home.pointerCursor.hyprcursor. Avoid shipping Posy (CC-BY-NC) or anime cursors (NC or unlicensed) in a distributable default.

Fonts: Maple Mono NF CN (nixpkgs maple-mono.NF-CN-unhinted; archlinuxcn ttf-maplemono-nf-cn-unhinted) for terminal and code. Nunito or Quicksand for UI (both packaged; Google Sans Flex with the ROND axis is nicer but you would have to package it yourself on Nix). Noto Color Emoji, Material Symbols Rounded for bar icons, and Noto Sans CJK plus LXGW WenKai for CJK.

Login and boot chain: SilentSDDM catppuccin-mocha (flake/AUR) or sddm-astronaut pixel_sakura (nixpkgs sddm-astronaut embeddedTheme), then Limine with the catppuccin-mocha-pink palette plus your own wallpaper (or catppuccin-grub if you stay on GRUB), then catppuccin-plymouth mocha (plymouth-blahaj-theme as an optional cute alternative).

Terminal cuteness: fastfetch with a kitty-direct PNG logo (works in Kitty and Ghostty) plus a command-raw fallback to pokemon-colorscripts or krabby. Add cbonsai, cava, pipes-rs and asciiquarium; all are in Arch (extra or AUR) and nixpkgs.

Apps: textfox (home-manager module) plus Catppuccin Firefox Color, spicetify-nix themes.catppuccin mocha, Vesktop with catppuccin-mocha-pink @import (or midnight catppuccin flavor), catppuccin nvim/VS Code (rose-pine dawn or kanagawa-lotus for light mode).
Sounds: ship the elementary sound theme (public domain) as the default notification sound set. Any cute or custom sounds should be user-supplied or CC0-sourced.

Wallpapers: only commit artwork you own or that is explicitly CC0/CC-BY with attribution. Write a fetch-at-install script with a per-image source URL and license manifest for the community repos (orangci, D3Ext, dharmx, gruvbox, rose-pine anime/manga sections) and for any anime art. Never vendor them into the repo. The same rule applies to anime SDDM/GRUB/Plymouth assets.
deprecations_pitfalls: catppuccin/gtk was archived 2024-06-02, but AUR catppuccin-gtk-theme-<flavor> and nixpkgs catppuccin-gtk still package it. catppuccin/nix's gtk module now only sets icons.

nixpkgs dropped gtk-engine-murrine and roughly 50 dependent GTK themes on 2026-07-22 (graphite-gtk-theme, vimix-gtk-themes, rose-pine-gtk-theme, kanagawa-gtk-theme, tokyonight-gtk-theme, lavanda/layan, sweet, materia-theme...). On Arch, gtk-engine-murrine and gtk-engines are AUR-only.
nixpkgs `noto-fonts-emoji` now throws; use `noto-fonts-color-emoji`. `maple-mono` is an attrset (maple-mono.NF-CN etc.), not a single package.
googlefonts/lexend, rubik, nunito and comfortaa source repos are archived. The fonts still exist in google/fonts. Comfortaa, Quicksand and Lexend carry Reserved Font Names.

Google Sans Flex is not in nixpkgs yet: the google-fonts rev pinned 2026-03-13 lacks ofl/googlesansflex, and there is no by-name attr. The AUR package is brand new (2026-09-25) and fetches an unpinned main-branch file.
The AUR sddm-astronaut-theme PKGBUILD (2025-01) lags upstream (2026-09). nixpkgs sddm-astronaut is current. Animated presets need qt6-multimedia (Arch qt6-multimedia-ffmpeg) and Qt >= 6.8.
SilentSDDM is not in nixpkgs; use its flake. Its default 'rei', 'ken' and 'silvia' presets use copyrighted anime backgrounds.
adi1090x/plymouth-themes has had no commits since 2023-08. Installing all of it via nixpkgs pulls about 524M, so always set selected_themes.
ShyFox's README says it is unmaintained and may break. Cascade was handed to a community org. catppuccin/firefox is only Firefox Color links (last commit 2023).
Posy cursor ports are CC-BY-NC-4.0 and anime-cursors art is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: non-commercial only. ctrlcat0xx/cursors and chihuahua-sound-theme have no license at all.

The wallpaper repos' LICENSE files (MIT/CC0) do not cover the third-party artwork inside them. rose-pine/wallpapers contradicts itself (CC0 file vs 'CC BY-SA 4.0' README). Anime GRUB, Plymouth and SDDM assets are character IP. Download these at install time, never redistribute them.

fastfetch kitty-direct works only in Kitty, Ghostty, WezTerm and Warp (PNG only in Kitty and Ghostty), not in Konsole. The kitty and sixel types need an imagemagick-enabled build. The command-raw logo requires fastfetch >= 2.45.0.

Several AUR -git theme PKGBUILDs are years old (e.g. grub-theme-vimix-*-git 2022, catppuccin-*-grub-theme-git 2022, reversal-icon-theme-git 2021, plymouth-theme-*-git 2020). They build from git HEAD, but their metadata is stale.

Unverified: Arch/AUR/nixpkgs packaging for the anime GRUB and Plymouth themes, Zen Maru Gothic, Elegant grub on AUR, and ocean-sound-theme's license. Also unverified: whether catppuccin/cursors v2 release assets include hyprcursor builds. I made no GitHub REST API calls; status comes from commits.atom feeds and repo HTML.
